column4: REFUTED: Granny 1.x (.GRN) does NOT use GR2s string-based OOD type system -- every distinctive Granny member-name string is absent from models.pak, so there is no self-describing shortcut to locating vertex arrays; the numeric 0xCA5E.... tags ARE the 1.x type system and must be mapped empirically
column5: Hypothesis from wigolo web research (RAD Granny3D docs via deepwiki sigmaco/granny3d-v2.7.0.30 and ragnarokresearchlab.github.io/file-formats/gr2): GR2 uses a "pointer fix-up" model (pointers stored as file-relative offsets, patched via a relocation table at load) plus an OOD (Object-Oriented Data) type system in which every structure carries a type definition with STRING member names. Prediction stated BEFORE measuring: if the 12-byte tagged-record stream in .GRN entries is an OOD type-descriptor table, models.pak must contain Grannys standard member-name strings. Measured over the full 434,340,164-byte models.pak: Position=0, TextureCoordinates=0, VertexData=0, TriTopology=0, PrimaryVertexData=0, PrimaryTopology=0, BoneBindings=0, BoneWeights=0, BoneIndices=0, Indices=0, Vertices=0, Tangent=0, Binormal=0, ArtToolInfo=0, FromFileName=0, VertexComponentNames=0, MaterialBindings=0, Groups=0, TriIndices=0, MeshName=0, ParentIndex=0, InverseWorld4x4=0, LODError=0. Non-zero hits are explained noise, not type descriptors: Bone=34380 and Mesh=739 are 3ds Max object-name substrings (Bone01 etc.), Normal=6 in 434MB is noise, Models/Meshes/Animations are English words in paths. CONCLUSION: the OOD string-table shortcut does not exist in 1.x -- consistent with RAD shipping a grn2gr2 CONVERTER, i.e. .GRN to .gr2 was a format change and not a version bump. CONSEQUENCE for the vertex hunt: no member-name search can locate the vertex arrays; the 56 numeric 0xCA5E tag families must be mapped empirically, and the pointer-fix-up insight still stands as the best structural lead (the trailing index/offset table near the terminator is a strong relocation-table candidate -- resolving its entries as file-relative offsets is the recommended next experiment). NEXT RESOURCE not yet read: the OpenGR2 wiki at github.com/arves100/opengr2/wiki/File-Format-documentation, referenced by Ragnarok Research Lab as the best public description.

column4: BREAKTHROUGH: Granny vertex data LOCATED -- it sits immediately after the node-name/string table, as RAW UNTAGGED float32 in the "root sector"; it carries no signature of its own by design, which is exactly why every prior signature-based scan failed
column5: Unblocks Phase 3 R1.2. Path: wigolo web research -> OpenGR2 wiki (github-wiki-see.page/m/arves100/opengr2/wiki/File-Format-documentation) documents that a Granny file splits into a TYPE SECTOR (node names, children, node type, array flag; 22 basic node types) and a ROOT SECTOR holding "the raw value of the data expressed in the type sector", with the explicit warning: "there is no direct association in the type sector to where the data is, so you have to parse the data from the type sector". That is precisely why rows 401-411 could not find vertices by scanning -- raw root-sector values are unrecognisable in isolation BY DESIGN. Corroborating: the wiki states GR2s key-value nodes ARE the GRN (Granny1) nodes, so the 0xCA5E tags are that node system; documented NodeInfo struct is {u32 type; ptrdiff_t name_offset; ptrdiff_t children_offset; u32 array_size; u8 unknown[12]; ptrdiff_t unknown2} = 32 bytes on 32-bit, matching the 32-byte root tag our walker already measured. LOCATION EVIDENCE: dumping printable strings from GLADIATOR.GRN (entry start abs 45197082, len 186842) recovered the real node vocabulary -- RAD 3D Studio MAX 4.x, 1.2b, 10-4-2000, win32, RAD copyright, __Standard, __FileName, __ObjectName, __Description, __Root, the source path D:\\New_Sacred\\Gladiator\\...\\Gladiator_mapping.max, mesh/material names Gladiator_Head, Gladiator_body, Gladiator_boots, Gladiator_Legs01, .tga texture paths, submesh names head/body/arm/hand/legs/boots, and bones Root/Bone_weapon_01/02 -- followed by apparent ASCII garbage dense in the bytes @ (0x40), B (0x42), C (0x43), which are IEEE-754 float32 EXPONENT high bytes for magnitudes 2-4, 32-64 and 128-256 respectively. Decoding entry-rel 18282 onward as little-endian float32 triples: 68 percent in-band, bbox x[-11.28,77.84] y[-10.32,7.84] z[-16.49,22.42] over 7998 triples. FALSIFIABILITY CONTROLS RUN (the projects own rule): the string table itself decodes to bbox +/-9778, a random mid-file offset to +/-7496 -- both garbage, proving the bbox test CAN fail; and BAT.GRN, a different and much smaller model, yields its own tight but DIFFERENT box x[-10.05,54.76] y[-1.68,54.76] z[-26.12,48.38]. HONEST LIMIT: the region is located and is definitely float geometry, but the exact stride/format is NOT yet confirmed -- GLADIATORs y-extent (18) versus x-extent (89) is asymmetric for a humanoid, which suggests the data may be interleaved (position+normal+UV) rather than pure XYZ triples, scrambling the naive 3-float grouping. NEXT: determine stride by cross-checking against the 385-triangle index table (row 408, references ~625 vertices) and by testing strides 3/6/8 floats.

column4: GRN sector boundaries decoded: type sector is only 1430 bytes, root sector is the other 185412 -- and this reconciles the two offset bases used in earlier rows
column5: grn_tagwalk --entry=589 (GLADIATOR.GRN, true_len 186842) consumes just 1430 bytes: magic at entry-rel 1258, 10 tags, terminator 0xca5effff at 1426. Everything from 1430 to EOF (185412 bytes) is the untagged root sector, exactly matching the OpenGR2 wiki type-sector/root-sector split logged in row 419. DECISIVE RECONCILIATION: row 408 reported the 385-record table at bulk-rel 179216; it is actually at entry-rel 180646, and 180646-179216 = 1430 exactly. So bulk-rel in rows 401-411 means ROOT-SECTOR-relative, while entry-rel in row 419 means entry-start-relative. The two coordinate systems differ by exactly the type-sector end, which is why the vertex-candidate offset 18282 (entry-rel) is 16852 in bulk-rel terms. Also decoded: root tag 0xca5e0000 payload field[3] = 185584 = true_len - 1258 = byte count from magic to EOF, a self-consistent size field. Header tags 0xca5e0101/0102/0103 carry {0, size, u32, 0} with sizes 185620/156/440.

column4: Row 408 was WRONG: the 385-record table is NOT a triangle/face index buffer -- two independent lines of evidence
column5: Row 408 read the 385x4 u32 table at root-rel 179216 as 385 triangles indexing ~625 vertices. Both halves fail. (1) CENSUS: the 1155 index slots cover exactly all 624 values 0..623 with none unused, but mean usage is 1.85 and 413 of 624 indices appear exactly ONCE. A real shared-vertex triangle mesh averages ~6 uses per vertex (each vertex ringed by ~6 faces); 1.85 with a majority of singletons is structurally incompatible with a face list. (2) EXHAUSTIVE GEOMETRIC SCAN: stated before measuring -- if these were triangles over a float array, some (base,stride) would connect NEARBY points, giving median_edge/bbox_diagonal about 0.02-0.15, versus about 0.35-0.50 for a random cloud. Scanned every base offset across the whole 186842-byte entry at strides 3,4,6,8,12,16 float32 in ALL FOUR byte-phases, plus int16 at strides 3,4,6,8, with a non-degeneracy guard (median edge > 1 percent of diagonal, under 5 percent zero-length edges, every axis at least 5 percent of the diagonal). column4: Two self-inflicted instrument failures in the stride scan, in OPPOSITE directions -- neither first result was a real measurement
column5: Logging these because the project rule is that a test which cannot fail proves nothing, and I built one of each. ATTEMPT 1 reported 0 candidates below 0.25 and I nearly recorded that as a refutation; it was an artifact of vetoing any candidate whose MAXIMUM absolute coordinate exceeded 1000, so a single outlier float killed otherwise-valid windows. ATTEMPT 2 relaxed that to a 98th-percentile test and then reported min_score=0.0000 -- a PERFECT fit -- at nearly every stride and byte-phase. That was the opposite failure: runs of repeated or zero floats make all 624 vertices coincide, so median triangle edge is literally 0 and the normalized score is 0. The metric had become a test that could not fail. Only ATTEMPT 3, adding an explicit non-degeneracy floor (median edge > 1 percent of diagonal, under 5 percent zero-length edges, genuine extent on all three axes), was capable of both passing and failing -- and it returned nothing, which is the result row 421 rests on. Do not trust a scan score without first asking what it returns on constant data.

column4: The GRN header size/value triples are not CRC32 -- cheap exhaustive test, zero matches
column5: Tags 0xca5e0102/0103/0101 carry payloads {0, 156, 733939242, 0}, {0, 440, 339201763, 0}, {0, 185620, 3792610267, 0, 6, 0, 156, 0}, which read naturally as {reserved, section_size, checksum, reserved}. Tested by sliding each (size, value) pair over every byte offset in the entry and computing zlib.crc32 of the size-length window. All three: ZERO matches out of ~186k positions each. The third field is therefore not a CRC32 of any contiguous same-length region of this entry. It may be a different checksum (Adler-32, RAD-proprietary), a CRC over decompressed rather than stored bytes, or not a checksum at all. Note 185620 also exceeds the 185412-byte root sector, so the sizes are not plain in-file section extents either.

The root bone's parent field holds its OWN index (0), NOT -1 as the published ptasev parser assumes (it accepts parentIndex >= -1 and would read bone 0 as a self-loop). GRN stores NO inverse-world bind matrix. The bone block ends flush against the next directory node in all three entries (BAT ends rel 29152 / next 29152; SHOULDER 34436 / 34436; GLADIATOR 155520 / 155520, gap 0 in every case) and no region of bone_count*64 bytes (2432 / 4800 / 4352) exists nearby. MeshWeights (0xCA5E0702) layout: int32 count, int32 highestBoneIndex, int32 unused, then per vertex int32 influenceCount followed by influenceCount x (int32 mesh-local bone, float32 weight). Confirmed by exact byte accounting, not by plausibility: bytes consumed equalled the node's derived span with ZERO slack on all five blocks (BAT node 527 span 1992 count 149; SHOULDER node 1008 span 1420 count 112; GLADIATOR nodes 1020/1030/1040 spans 7356/2760/3188 counts 448/213/232), every vertex's weights summed to 1.0 within 1e-4, and the observed max mesh-local bone equalled the declared highestBoneIndex exactly. Mesh-local bone indices resolve to Granny file bone indices through the 0xCA5E0C0A FormMeshBone children of a 0xCA5E0C09 FormMeshBoneSection, each a single int32. The pairing to a mesh is NOT positional -- FormMeshBoneSection order does not follow Mesh order -- it is the section whose child count equals that mesh's highestBoneIndex + 1. That rule matched uniquely in every case (15 vs 14, 5 vs 4, and GLADIATOR's 45/4/10 vs 44/3/9), and the port re-checks uniqueness at run time and refuses rather than picking one when two sections could match

REST_BIND_EPS is DERIVED, not chosen: eps = f32_ulp(maxmag) * 4 ULPs * (max_chain_depth + 2), with every input measured from the file. GLADIATOR.GRN maxmag=110.000 ulp=0.000007629 depth=15 -> eps=0.000518799; GLAD_SA5_SHOULDER.GRN maxmag=65.442 ulp=0.000007629 depth=15 -> eps=0.000518799; BAT.GRN maxmag=54.759 ulp=0.000003815 depth=10 -> eps=0.000183105. maxmag is the largest absolute component over every composed bind basis column and origin; the ULP is the float32 gap at that magnitude; the depth factor is there because the chain is composed once per side and the comparison passes back through an inverse. All four numbers are printed beside every verdict on both harness sides. Sizing method carried over from findings row 368 (Phase 2 BAND_TIE_EPS).

The --grn=GLADIATOR render then REFUSED to draw: push_error 'entry 589 rest does not equal bind -- max component delta 0.005187988 against eps 0.000518799 (maxmag 110.000)', run exit 1 -- and 0.005187988 is exactly 10x eps, so the measured delta matches the injected offset. The two sides are asymmetric on purpose: Godot computes rest_eq_bind from the CONSTRUCTED Skeleton3D and Skin via ModelView.rig_facts (the production rig builder, not a harness reimplementation), Python computes it from an independent float64 decode of the stored bytes. layer files=7 violations=0; md5sum install/pak/models.pak unchanged at 45ff42c9ec2c8ce73226a00330fd7282.

Godot float32 and Python float64 chain composition MEASURABLY DIVERGE, and the fact line's precision was set by that error budget rather than by what made the diff pass. GLAD_SA5_SHOULDER.GRN maxmag: 65.442268372 (Godot, float32 Transform3D) vs 65.442287861 (Python, float64) -- a difference of 1.95e-5 accumulated over a depth-15 chain, which is the same order as the depth x ULP budget eps itself is built from. maxmag is therefore printed at %.3f on both sides: nine decimals would be asserting digits the number does not have. eps, ulp and depth ARE exact on both sides and are printed at full precision -- ulp is a power of two, depth an integer, and the two magnitudes land in the same binade so they yield the same ULP. Bit-emulating Godot's Basis::set_quaternion in Python was considered and REJECTED: it would test the arithmetic library rather than the decode, and it would make the Python side a translation of the Godot side instead of an independent implementation.

rest_eq_bind AS SHIPPED IN PLAN 06 IS CIRCULAR AND PROVES NOTHING ABOUT THE BIND POSE. Withdrawing the row-472 claim's scope. Traced in code, not inferred: model_view.gd:279 sets each bone's rest from the stored LOCAL transform bl[g].rest; line 331 reads got = Skeleton3D.get_bone_global_rest(), which is Godot's chain product of those local rests; line 332 reads want = binds[g], which is Sacred.Models.bind_poses()'s OWN chain product of THE SAME local rests. Both operands descend from one stored source, which is exactly what the Plan 06 prohibition forbids -- the check compares two implementations of matrix multiplication, not a construction against an independent expectation. This is why delta was EXACTLY 0.000000000 across 68 bones of float32 work: same inputs, same ops, same order. Worse, line 312 adds the Skin bind as binds[g].affine_inverse(), so the skin matrix is got * want^-1 = identity BY CONSTRUCTION for ANY bone data whatsoever, including wrong data. Measured: bind*bind^-1 within 1.2e-5 of identity. CONSEQUENCE: the whole Plan 06 skeleton/skin layer is a mathematical no-op in bind pose and CANNOT change the picture; rest_eq_bind=true is not evidence the skeleton is right. The ten-times-epsilon perturbation (row 472) remains valid but proves only that the COMPARISON discriminates, never that the operands were independent. No independent bind matrix exists in the file to compare against (established in Plan 06 Task 1), so this cannot be repaired by editing the assertion -- it needs re-planning.

THE PLAN 06 HANDEDNESS ORACLE IS A TEST THAT CANNOT FAIL. Plan 06 Task 3 states its premise as 'a single shoulder guard is worn on one arm, so a mirrored coordinate matrix puts it on the wrong side'. That premise is FALSE. GLAD_SA5_SHOULDER.GRN contains BOTH guards: two welded components of exactly 81 verts each, from the same Mesh node, separated by 8.6203 units (23.43% of its 36.79 diagonal), and mirror-symmetric about Y. Reflection test, worst nearest-neighbour distance after reflecting component 0 onto component 1: Y axis 0.24245, against X 23.26602 and Z 21.30190 -- a 96x separation, so the Y reading is not a coincidence of a sparse shell. A model that is its own Y-mirror renders IDENTICALLY under a Y-mirrored coordinate matrix, so this capture cannot detect the defect it was chosen to detect. The human's 'unusable as a handedness oracle in this state' is confirmed, with the cause: not a decode failure but the wrong subject. It also explains the 'two disconnected fragments floating apart' -- that is the left and right guard with the torso's width between them, which is retail truth. A genuinely asymmetric single-sided asset is required instead, and the phase's handedness edge is UNCOVERED until one is found.

RAD Granny Viewer CANNOT serve as the render oracle for GLADIATOR with the binaries on this machine. Root cause established, not guessed: /tmp/smdl/gr2_viewer.exe self-identifies in its own about panel as "Granny Viewer 2.2.0.4 (C) 1999-2002 RAD Game Tools", and its PE import table lists ONLY WINMM/KERNEL32/USER32/GDI32/SHELL32/COMCTL32/comdlg32/OPENGL32 -- no granny2.dll and no grn2gr2.dll, so its Granny runtime is STATICALLY LINKED at 2.2 and cannot be upgraded by swapping the 2.5.0.11 or 2.7.0.30 DLLs sitting beside it. Both inputs are rejected at load with the modal "File \"%s\" failed its CRC check, and is likely corrupted.": GLADIATOR.GRN directly, and g27/out.gr2 (the granny 2.7 conversion). out.gr2 is NOT corrupt -- its stored header CRC 0x4ec02995 is a bit-exact standard CRC-32 over bytes [104:59480], and its header fileSize field 59480 equals the actual byte length, so the file is internally self-consistent under granny 2.7 conventions (file version field = 7). The 2.2 reader therefore CRCs a different byte range because its section layout expectation differs, which is a file-format-version mismatch surfacing as a CRC message. Corroborated by RAD-derived documentation for gr2_viewer.exe: "if the file fails to open in the viewer, the export or preprocessing step is corrupted, or there is a version mismatch between the file and the granny2.dll used by the viewer". No v6 writer exists on this machine: grn2gr2.dll has no granny2.dll import string, so it writes version 7 unconditionally regardless of which granny2.dll is placed next to it.

GRANNY 2.7.0.30 ORACLE COUNTS FOR GLADIATOR, re-measured this session by re-running g27/gh7.exe under wine rather than trusting the prior log, and reproduced identically across two runs. 3 meshes, all name=(unnamed). mesh0 vertices=280 indices=1155 triangles=385; mesh1 vertices=609 indices=2604 triangles=868; mesh2 vertices=307 indices=1326 triangles=442. TOTALS vertices=1196 triangles=1695 indices=5085. Against our decoder (933 verts / 1695 tris / 68 bones / 56 binds / 3 mesh nodes): TRIANGLE COUNT MATCHES EXACTLY at 1695 and MESH COUNT MATCHES at 3, but OUR VERTEX COUNT IS SHORT BY 263 (933 vs 1196, we have 78.0% of granny). Triangle parity with a vertex deficit means our index buffer is intact and correctly sized while our vertex array is being collapsed -- the likely cause is de-duplication of positions that granny keeps distinct because they differ in a non-position channel. Granny reports the vertex layout as Position(f32x3 @+0), BoneWeights(width4 @+12), BoneIndices(width4 @+16), Normal(f32x3 @+24), TextureCoordinates0(f32x2 @+36), with GrannyGetTotalObjectSize AUTHORITATIVE = 40 bytes (not the 44 a naive offset sum gives) and bytesPerIndex=4. Split vertices at UV or normal seams are the first hypothesis to test for the missing 263. Bone count was NOT measured -- no harness on disk dumps the skeleton, so 68 bones and 56 binds remain UNCORROBORATED by granny.

UP AXIS IS +Y, ESTABLISHED BY EXTERNAL RENDER -- resolves the deliberately-unlocated basis of row 453. ptasev's GRN viewer renders GLADIATOR.GRN STANDING FULLY UPRIGHT on its ground grid in the DEFAULT view, before any camera control was touched, and remains upright through two 180-degree orbits. Corroborated numerically and independently of the render by the viewer's own per-mesh bounding boxes, which order the three meshes head-over-heels along Y exactly as anatomy requires: legs/boots mesh Y[-4.0335,44.1928], body mesh Y[32.3761,71.5712], head mesh Y[61.9141,77.8393] -- a monotone foot-to-crown climb in Y with the feet at Y~0. The lateral axes are correspondingly shallow (body X span 15.78, Z span 32.76) against a total Y height of ~77.8. So the file is authored Y-up with the ground plane at Y=0, and OUR RENDER LYING ON ITS SIDE IS OUR BASIS BUG, NOT THE DATA. This is the evidence row 453 refused to insert a corrective rotation without.

THIRD INDEPENDENT VERTEX COUNT IS 893, AND IT DECIDES THE 1196-VS-933 QUESTION AGAINST BOTH OF US. ptasev's viewer reports per mesh (matched to granny by triangle count, which agrees exactly in all three): t=868 body verts=448, t=385 head verts=213, t=442 legs verts=232, TOTAL vertices=893, total faces=1695. Three-way table -- granny 2.7.0.30 1196 / ours 933 / viewer 893, with triangles 1695 in ALL THREE and meshes 3 in all three. The viewer's debug console states the mechanism outright: 'MeshTriangles face layout: [vertA,vertB,vertC, normA,normB,normC] (6x int32, 24 bytes/face)' -- each face corner carries a SEPARATE position index and normal index, and per mesh it reports verts=448/norms=447, verts=213/norms=255, verts=232/norms=231, flagging 'normCount!=vertCount (split normals -- hard edges present)'. UV counts are larger still: 3218+624+703 = 4545 UVs against 5085 face corners. So 893 is the raw POSITION array length, 1196 is granny's count of unique (position,normal,UV) tuples after de-indexing and re-welding, and the 303-vertex gap between them is exactly the seam splitting granny performs and the viewer does not. Our 933 sits BETWEEN the two and therefore matches neither model: we are neither reading the raw position arrays (893) nor performing granny's full seam split (1196), which means the earlier row-488 hypothesis 'our vertex array is being collapsed' is the wrong shape -- we are partially splitting. The fix is to pick a lane: read 893 positions and split per unique (pos,norm,uv) corner tuple to reach 1196.

68 BONES CORROBORATED EXTERNALLY FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THE 12 UNBOUND BONES ARE EXPLAINED. ROW 491'S MECHANISM FOR 1196 IS WRONG IN INDEX SPACE, AND THE UV INDICES ARE NOT IN THE FACE RECORD. Row 491 asserted 1196 is 'granny's count of unique (position,normal,UV) tuples after de-indexing'; that was an inference, and measuring it refutes it. First, the UV indices were located: they are NOT in the 24-byte face record (which carries position and normal indices only), but in ModelSection 0xCA5E0E01 > Model > RenderPassSection > RenderPass, whose leaf child holds {int32 count} then count x {int32 faceIndex, int32 uvA, int32 uvB, int32 uvC}. A RenderPass names a FormMesh SLOT, not a mesh: its first int32 indexes the FormMesh 0xCA5E0C03 list whose own first int32 is a 1-based mesh ordinal -- for GLADIATOR that map is [2,0,1], so slot and mesh are NOT equal and a positional assumption would have silently swapped body for legs. All 1695 faces resolve a UV triple, 6 RenderPasses over 3 meshes (212+230 -> legs, 260+258+350 -> body, 385 -> head). The UV values themselves are in MeshField 0xCA5E0803 under MeshFieldSection 0xCA5E0804: layout is {u32 componentCount} + N x 3 x float32, with componentCount = 3 in all four fields and (span-4)/12 exact in all four (2322, 896, 624, 703). Mesh 0 carries TWO fields, 2322+896 = 3218, and the per-mesh totals 3218/624/703 = 4545 reproduce the external viewer's UV counts exactly. With those indices in hand, EVERY index-space grouping was censused in one pass and NOT ONE lands on 1196: p=887, q=933, uv=3649, p+q=933, p+uv=3715, q+uv=3755, p+q+uv=3755, and adding a render-pass namespace gives pass:p=935, pass:q=981, pass:p+q=981, pass:p+q+uv=3755. Our 933 is p+q. The (position,normal,UV) index tuple overshoots by more than 3x.

1196 IS A VALUE-SPACE WELD, NOT AN INDEX-SPACE ONE, AND IT REPRODUCES GRANNY PER MESH. Prediction stated before measuring, from row 445's unexplained '624 -> 280': if the arrays store the same value at many indices, a converter welding by VALUE would collapse far below the index-tuple count. Measured: distinct (position, normal, UV) VALUE tuples over the corner list give per mesh 609 / 279 / 307 against granny 2.7.0.30's 609 / 280 / 307, total 1195 against 1196. Two of the three meshes are EXACT and the third is short by exactly one vertex. The per-mesh match is the load-bearing part: a total that agreed while the per-mesh split disagreed would be a coincidence, and this is the opposite. Keys were taken on raw float32 BIT PATTERNS, not on formatted decimals -- an earlier %.6f key merged genuinely distinct positions (mesh 1 read 207 instead of 209) though it happened not to move the tuple total. The residual 1 vertex on the head is NOT explained and is not fudged: no channel remains in granny's declared layout that could split it, since bone weights and indices are keyed on position and would add no split. It is 0.08% of the model and is recorded as an open discrepancy, not rounded away. Also measured: keying position by INDEX rather than by value gives the identical 609/279/307, so the implementation uses the index (which cannot merge two coincident vertices whose bone weights differ) at zero cost in count.

COORDINATE BASIS LOCATED BY DERIVATION AND CONFIRMED AGAINST THE EXTERNAL ORACLE TO FOUR DECIMALS. The basis is NOT stored in the file: an exhaustive scan of the header and node directory for nine consecutive orthonormal float32 returns zero hits, so it had to be derived from geometry rather than read. Derivation, stated before any image was looked at: the external render's per-mesh boxes climb foot-to-crown along ITS up axis as legs [-4.0335,44.1928], body [32.3761,71.5712], head [61.9141,77.8393]; computing the same boxes from our own decode reproduces those intervals on our STORED COMPONENT 2 and on neither other component, so component 2 is up and (X,Y,Z) = (x,z,y). That bare mapping is a reflection (determinant -1) which would silently mirror the asset, so the determinant +1 member of the pair is used: the -90 degree rotation about X, (x,y,z) -> (x,z,-y), Basis columns (1,0,0),(0,0,-1),(0,1,0). Verified after implementing, from our own arrays and before viewing any PNG: Godot-space per-mesh Y intervals are legs [-4.0335,44.1928], body [32.3761,71.5712], head [61.9141,77.8393] -- EXACT agreement with the oracle on all three meshes to 4 decimals, monotone climb, feet at ~0, determinant +1.000. HANDEDNESS IS STILL NOT CLAIMED: the GLAD_SA5_SHOULDER oracle intended to settle it is its own Y-mirror (row 480) and cannot fail, so it settles nothing. What the bbox evidence also does not fix is one rotation about the up axis, the facing direction; that is a separate question from handedness and remains open.

WHY NO SITE COULD HAVE PASSED: OVERHEAD GEOMETRY CANNOT OCCLUDE A GROUND-ANCHORED MARKER IN THIS RENDERER. A roof over a walkable cell is anchored behind that cell, so its band depth is farther, so it is submitted first and the cube draws over it -- for any site, any zoom. SURVEY OF unpack-tools/Granny_Modelling: FIVE TOOLS, ONE USEFUL DOCUMENT. ExportTool, evegr2toobj.2, gr2meshconv1_3, grnreader98.v1.4.0.3.debug and the gr2_viewer bundle are all granny2.dll wrappers -- they delegate parsing to RAD's proprietary Windows runtime rather than decoding the container, so none is portable to a Linux/Godot runtime (and none is copyable: clean-room rule). The one artefact of value is gr2meshconv1_3/src/structs.pl, which does not declare structs but SCRAPES the type table out of gr2_viewer.exe at 0x5312d8 -- i.e. the Granny runtime carries a reflection type tree, and Granny files are self-describing, so a parser reads layout from the file rather than hardcoding it. Corroborates the GRN parser found at row 444. structs.h names the types a character pipeline needs: t_Skeleton, t_VertexData, t_TriangleIndices, t_Mesh, t_BoneBindings, t_TrackGroups, t_OrientationCurve, t_MorphTargets. CAVEAT NOT YET TESTED: these tools target GR2 (evegr2toobj is EVE Online specific) while Sacred ships .grn, the older container; the type-tree concept should carry, the container framing may not. Nothing here was checked against a Sacred file.

HERODUMP SOURCE FULLY DOCUMENTS SACRED'S HERO/SAVEGAME 'PAX' CONTAINER -- FIRST unpack-tools ENTRY WITH NO PROPRIETARY DEPENDENCY. Layout read from SacredHeroFile.cpp tPaxHeader/tSectionEntry/tSection: 256-byte header (3-byte magic, 1-byte header version, u32 section count, 9 unlabelled u32, 212 zero bytes) then a section table at 0x0100 of 12-byte entries {u32 type, u32 offset, u32 size_uncompressed}; each section begins with a 32-byte header {u32 signature, u32 size_compressed, 24 zero bytes} followed by payload, where signature 0xBAADC0DE marks zlib deflate and sections are inflated via zlib. Sections are keyed by type id into a map -- a tagged-chunk container, the same shape as Sacred's other formats. Sole dependency is zlib, which Godot provides; the Win32 calls in Load() are plain file I/O, not format logic. NOT VERIFIED: the 9 header DWORDs are unlabelled and no Sacred hero file has been parsed against this layout here -- documentation of behaviour only, clean-room rule applies. Scope note: this is the SAVE/LOAD path, unrelated to the runtime rendering data and to the row-502 sort-key defect.

github.com/sigmaco/granny3d-v2.7.0.30 is the genuine RAD Granny 2.7.0.30 SDK drop (2007-12-01): include/granny.h 318KB with every format struct, doc/granny2.chm, AND exporters/plugins/win32/grn2gr2.dll -- the same converter our oracle harness already uses. Container layer is now fully documented, no byte-guessing needed. granny_grn_file_magic_value (32B, PRECEDES header): u32 MagicValue[4], u32 HeaderSize, u32 HeaderFormat, u32 Reserved[2]. granny_grn_file_header: u32 Version, TotalSize, CRC, SectionArrayOffset, SectionArrayCount, then grn_reference RootObjectTypeDefinition + grn_reference RootObject, u32 TypeTag, u32 ExtraTags[4], u32 StringDatabaseCRC, u32 ReservedUnused[3]. GrannyCurrentGRNStandardTag = 0x80000000+38 = 0x80000026. granny_grn_section = 11 x u32 = 44B: Format, DataOffset, DataSize, ExpandedDataSize, InternalAlignment, First16Bit, First8Bit, PointerFixupArrayOffset, PointerFixupArrayCount, MixedMarshallingFixupArrayOffset, MixedMarshallingFixupArrayCount. Section.Format is granny_compression_type {0=None, 1=Oodle0, 2=Oodle1} -- same DataSize-vs-ExpandedDataSize pattern as PAX (row 508). Eight fixed section indices: Main=0, RigidVertex=1, RigidIndex=2, DeformableVertex=3, DeformableIndex=4, Texture=5, Discardable=6, Unloaded=7. Pointers are NOT file offsets: granny_grn_reference = {u32 SectionIndex, u32 Offset}, relocated via the per-section PointerFixup array (granny_grn_pointer_fixup = {u32 FromOffset, grn_reference To}).

granny_tri_topology carries TWO INDEPENDENT index arrays with separate counts: int32 IndexCount/Indices AND int32 Index16Count/uint16 Indices16. A parser that reads one and ignores the other sees a different triangle set -- this is the structural fact the rows 418-443 stride-guessing was circling. Triangles are further partitioned by granny_tri_material_group {int32 MaterialIndex, TriFirst, TriCount}, so 'mesh 0' in any tool is a TriFirst/TriCount slice, not the whole mesh. Topology also carries VertexToVertexCount/VertexToVertexMap, which is the engine's own record of VERTEX SPLITTING -- the mechanism behind the 2026-08-08 'vertex split' observation. granny_mesh itself has no vertex count; it is granny_mesh.PrimaryVertexData.VertexData.VertexCount, and granny_vertex_data.VertexType is a data_type_definition pointer, confirming the self-describing type tree of row 507.

HYPOTHESIS STATED BEFORE MEASUREMENT (per project rule): the open 624-distinct-vertices-in-GRN-index-table vs 280-vertices-in-grn2gr2-GR2-mesh-0 discrepancy is NOT conversion loss. Two candidate mechanisms, both now documented in granny.h and both testable: (a) mesh 0 is one granny_tri_material_group slice (TriFirst/TriCount) of a multi-material topology, so 280 is a subset by construction; (b) our reader consumed Indices16 while the converter emitted Indices, or vice versa. TEST THAT CAN FAIL: dump GroupCount + every {MaterialIndex,TriFirst,TriCount} and BOTH IndexCount and Index16Count for GLADIATOR.GRN. If GroupCount==1 and one index count is 0, (a) is refuted and (b) is forced; if the group-0 TriCount*3 spans exactly 280 distinct indices, (a) is confirmed and no conversion bug exists. Predicted-if-false: a GroupCount of 1 with both index arrays populated would refute both.

Row 507 said the Granny type table had to be scraped out of gr2_viewer.exe at 0x5312d8 by structs.pl. That was the only route available from unpack-tools/Granny_Modelling, but it is not the best one: the same definitions are plain C source in include/granny.h in the 2.7.0.30 SDK drop, with GrannyTypeSizeCheck static assertions spelling out every field width. Prefer the header. LICENCE CAVEAT: the repo carries NO licence file and Granny is commercial RAD/Epic middleware, so it is documentation-of-behaviour ONLY under the standing clean-room rule -- read the struct layout, write the reader from our own bytes, copy nothing. Downloaded to /tmp, deliberately not into the repo.

Diffed unpack-tools/Granny_Common_2_11_8_0_Release/include/granny.h against the 2.7.0.30 header (rows 512-513). CONTAINER IS STABLE: granny_grn_file_header and granny_grn_section are byte-identical across 2.7.0.30 -> 2.11.8.0 (differences in the diff output were trailing whitespace from my own sed normalisation, not the source). granny_vertex_data and granny_mesh likewise unchanged. So the 44-byte section record and the header layout in row 512 are safe to hardcode for any Granny generation. Note 2.11 wraps definitions in a GRANNY_STRUCT(struct) macro where 2.7 used a bare 'struct' -- a grep for '^struct granny_' finds nothing in 2.11 and will read as 'the struct was removed' if you do not check the macro form first. I made exactly that error before re-running.

granny_tri_topology IS NOT VERSION-STABLE. 2.11.8.0 inserts four fields that 2.7.0.30 does not have -- int32 PolygonIndexStartCount, int32* PolygonIndexStarts, int32 PolygonIndexCount, int32* PolygonIndices -- positioned between SideToNeighborMap and BonesForTriangleCount. On a 32-bit build that shifts every field from BonesForTriangleCount onward by 16 bytes. Any reader that hardcodes the 2.11 topology layout will misparse a 2004-era Sacred .grn, and the corruption starts precisely at the bone-binding fields. GrannyCurrentGRNStandardTag also moves: 0x80000000+38 = 0x80000026 in 2.7.0.30, 0x80000000+57 = 0x80000039 in 2.11.8.0, so granny_grn_file_header.TypeTag identifies the exporter generation of any given file. CONSEQUENCE: this is positive evidence for the self-describing route of row 507 -- resolve fields through the file's own data_type_definition tree, never against a header snapshot. The header is for cross-checking what the tree says, not for substituting it.

Read granny_grn_file_header.TypeTag from a Sacred .grn (e.g. GLADIATOR.GRN) and compare against 0x80000026 (2.7.0.30) and 0x80000039 (2.11.8.0) to pin which exporter generation the retail assets came from. Cheap: one u32 at a fixed offset after the 32-byte magic block. This also gates row 514 -- if the tag predates 2.7 the topology layout may differ again and the 624-vs-280 test must read field offsets from the file's type tree rather than either header. PAX format fully read and independently confirmed against Hero00.pax. Header (SacredHeroFile.cpp tPaxHeader): BYTE[3]='AMH' + BYTE version=0x1B, u32 SectionCount at 0x04 (=16), nine u32 unknowns (u1=556 at 0x08, u6=1 at 0x1C), then 212 zero bytes. Section table at fixed offset 0x0100, SectionCount entries of 12 bytes: {u32 Type, u32 Offset, u32 SizeUncompressed}; Type==0 means unused slot. Section body at Offset: {u32 Signature, u32 SizeCompressed, 24 zero bytes} then payload at Offset+0x20 IF Signature==0xBAADC0DE (compressed); otherwise the payload is raw and starts at Offset itself with length SizeUncompressed. Special case: Type 0xC4 payload length is hardcoded to 64 regardless of the table value. Compression is plain zlib (inflateInit/inflate, no raw-deflate window hack).

Method note against row 536 and row 541. A control arm that matches only the RANGE of a candidate id set is not sufficient when the target table has non-uniform density and the ids are clustered -- it manufactures an apparent hit. Row 536 (items.pak sprite names) happened to survive this because its hypothesis scored BELOW its control, but the same uniform-range control would have produced a false positive had the numbers gone the other way, exactly as it did in row 541. Standing rule for future id-attribution tests in this project: the control must preserve the distribution of the real ids, not just their min/max. The cheap distribution-matched control is a SHIFT SWEEP (score id+k for several k); if k=0 does not beat the shifted variants, there is no alignment. Reported figures in row 541 differ slightly between the two runs (126 vs 135 of 184) because the first used a stricter "meaningful float" predicate that also excluded 0<|x|<1e-9; the shift sweep uses the looser predicate throughout so its columns are self-consistent.

0xC7 header mapped; it is the second per-hero-varying section after 0xC8 and the best remaining candidate for the character record. Sizes 2079/2167/2189/2189/2211/2211/2277/2365. Fixed header: u16@0 = 3990 in all eight, u16@2 = 0/0/0/1/1/0/0/1 (set for Dunkelelf, Kampfmagier, Daemonin -- a binary flag with no obvious class grouping, unattributed), u32@4 = 336242 and u32@8 = 207390 constant, u32@16 = 0xFEEDF00D, u32@20 = 3277185, u32@24 = 65536, u16@30 = class id. Unlike 0xC8, 0xFEEDF00D occurs exactly ONCE (at offset 16) and 0xBAADC0DE never occurs, so 0xC7 does not use the per-record sentinel framing of 0xC8; the single occurrence is a header marker. Record stride is BOUNDED not determined: gcd of the pairwise size differences is 22, so any stride must divide 22, i.e. 1, 2, 11 or 22. All eight sizes are odd multiples of 11. Do not quote 22 as the record size until a record boundary is exhibited -- gcd is an upper bound on the stride, not evidence of one. Head 58.5% identical over the 2079-byte overlap, common prefix 2 bytes, common suffix 6.

column4: ROOT CAUSE of missing chapel interior + partial roof cut: float32 precision collapse in the uv2.y shader-bucket channel. Not a data, level-parse, or classification bug. Rows 661/662 both survive as consequences.
column5: VERIFIED by direct measurement (godot-port/f32_probe.gd). sector_view.gd:534 computes bucket = region_key*2 + class_bit where region_key = gx*1000000 + gy*1000 + idx. At sector 50,39 region_key = 50039000, so INTERIOR bucket = 100078001, EXTERIOR = 100078000. sector_view.gd:560 writes bucket into uv2.y of a PackedVector2Array = a FLOAT32 vertex attribute. At 1.0e8 the float32 ULP is 8, so 100078001 snaps to 100078000. Measured: stored ext=100078000.0 int=100078000.0 collapsed=true; mesh roundtrip uv2.y=100078000.0 -> shader int 100078000. object.gdshader:66 does int b = int(bucket + 0.5) and therefore reads the EXTERIOR id for INTERIOR fragments. 728 of 777 objects in this sector are INTERIOR-classed and bound to that single region key, so --force-interior (which hides bucket rk*2 = 100078000) discards the interior geometry too and the whole chapel vanishes, leaving only terrain/paving which is a separate mesh. Exactly the reported symptom. SCOPE (VERIFIED): buckets survive only while rk*2+1 <= 2^24. Measured collapsed=false for gx=0,4,8; collapsed=true for gx=9,16,17,32,50,99. So the swap bucket encoding is intact ONLY for sectors with gx <= 8 - essentially the entire world is broken; every INTERIOR bucket aliases onto its own EXTERIOR bucket. RECONCILIATION of rows 661 vs 662: both agents were right. Port is_top_level() returns true for every _2_ sprite and _fam_top is computed over ALL items.pak defs and agrees with the census that top = level 2 - the level parse is CORRECT, my leading suspicion in row 662 was WRONG. Sector 50,39 loads 777 objects via +0x04; classification INTERIOR 728 / SHARED 27 / EXTERIOR 22; 64 KLOSTER_KAPELLE01 pieces in the rect, 30 of them level-2, all 30 classify INTERIOR with region_key 50039000 bucket 100078001. Census 47 vs probe 30 is not a disagreement, just a different containment test (near-footprint overhang which _footprint_membership also binds). ALSO REFUTED: the row 661 +0x0c hypothesis. Measured over 4096 cells: nonzero +0x04 = 777, nonzero +0x0c = 2145, both nonzero = 377, h0c == h04 = 0; +0x0c resolved via Statics.get_object() = 0 resolved / 2145 unresolved; 2146 distinct values each unique, ~5039270 -> ~50419xx, monotonically increasing with cell index in steps of 1-5. static.pak indices in this sector top out near 758k so every +0x0c value is out of range. HYPOTHESIS: +0x0c is a per-cell serial / global running id, not an object reference. NOTE this contradicts row 662s claim that +0x0c is zero for all 4096 cells (measured here: zero for 1951, nonzero for 2145, read via the same World.sector() path the port uses) - worth reconciling but does not change any verdict. Also +0x08 is 0x00000000 for all 4096 cells (1 distinct value).
column6: FIX DIRECTION (not yet applied): the bucket id must stop being a large integer smuggled through a float32 vertex channel. Option (a) is smallest. Second real bug from row 661 still open: apply_swap _force_interior collects region keys only from the band-first object of each run (sector_view.gd:496-506,790-798) so most region keys never enter the hidden set. RMS residual 243 cells = 3.80f the 6400-cell world span, max residual 822 cells (Alkazaba noc Draco), residuals structured with peripheral towns worst. Two structural HYPOTHESES worth keeping: (a) poster orientation MATCHES the community maps and is not rotated - poster +x tracks (gx-gy), poster +y tracks (gx+gy), and the (gx+gy) rows dependence on poster-x came out -0.024 ~= zero, so it is the same isometric-diamond view restretched to portrait despite the compass rose; (b) the poster covers only the inhabited core, not the full 6400x6400 grid - world corners project to px (366,-18),(1693,1217),(-488,1207),(839,2441) far outside the 1093x1657 frame while all 54 community towns project to x -9..991 y 200..1549 filling it neatly. IMPORTANT INDEPENDENT FINDING: the one hard anchor DISAGREES with the community map. Engine ground truth puts Silver Creek Cathedral at cell (3213,2502); the community pin "Silver Creek" sits at (3188,2808) - matching in gx but 306 cells off in gy. Label-vs-building offset explains some of that, not obviously all. This is independent of the PDF and qualifies row 658s cross-validation claim. column4: ROOF-CUTAWAY MECHANISM FOUND in Sacred.exe disassembly. Also: layers are height levels with one full sector each; static flags semantics REFUTED and replaced; WldxEntry +0x0c is a FLOOR.PAK handle; Resacred header off-by-four corrected.
column5: ROUTE: the .idb was UNNECESSARY, not blocked. The repo ALREADY CONTAINS a fully analyzed Ghidra project at analysis/ghidra/sacred-re.rep (669MB, 4 programs: Sacred.exe Gold 2.28 image base 0x400000 with 25246 functions matching the .idbs path, armalion.exe, sacred_orig, sacred-1.0.02-final). No import or re-analysis needed, headless queries ~30s each. Copied to /tmp/sacredre, repo untouched. ALSO analysis/symbols/armalion2001_demangled.txt has ~4700 REAL demangled C++ symbols from the 2001 prerelease incl cWorld::getPatchPtrLayered(cPatchPosition&,unsigned int), cSector::getHeightInfo, cSector::getPatch, cWorldView1::drawInit (names only, no addresses). FYI Sacred_2.idb is uncompressed IDA1 32-bit and strings yields 194k lines incl cWorld_getSectorInitialized_inBounds, WorldViewSub.staticId - names are plaintext but addresses need an id0 B-tree parser (python-idb not installed). CENTRAL FUNCTION: FUN_0062ae90 @ 0x0062ae90 = the world draw loop (cWorldView), reads every field we asked about. All addresses in Sacred.exe Gold 2.28. LAYERS ARE HEIGHT LEVELS (VERIFIED): cSector +0x70 numHeights u16, +0x74 height-chunk array stride 0x24, +0x78[i] per-layer info ptr; guarded by FUN_00622a80 "cSector::getHeightChunk Layer > numHeights" and FUN_00622ab0 "cSector::getHeightInfo Layer > numHeights"; FUN_006231a0 prints heightLevel[%d] per layer. Draw loop bounds-checks -1 < layer && layer < 9 then sector = *(int*)(view + 0x970b0 + layer*4) - an array of NINE SECTOR POINTERS, ONE PER LAYER. Patch array at sector+0x6c, patch index 0..0x1000 (4096=64x64), STRIDE 0x20. THE CUTAWAY (VERIFIED mechanism, HYPOTHESIS on purpose): it is a CONDITIONAL DEFERRED QUAD PASS keyed off someTypeId HIGH NIBBLE. Only the high nibble of patch +0x1f is ever tested (& 0xf0); observed constants 0x10, 0x20, 0x90, 0xa0. For 0x90/0xa0 the code fetches a byte from the sector: *(byte*)(*(int*)(sector+0x17c)+0xf7) for 0x90, +0xf8 for 0xa0 - so each sector carries TWO ZONE IDS and the nibble selects which one this patch belongs to. Patch is pushed to a deferred list at view+0x3ff2c stride 0x98, count at view+0x80e3c (record: patch ptr, screen x/y, sector-local tx/ty, LAYER, four 0x20-byte vertex blocks). Consumed by FUN_0062dd00 @ 0x0062dd00 which re-derives the zone id the same way and draws the quad ONLY IF *(char*)(engine + zoneId*0xd8 + 0x92b4) != 0 - an array of zone records stride 0xd8 each carrying a VISIBILITY BOOLEAN. Whole pass gated by DAT_0182ee78 < 2 (detail/quality global), uses alpha/blend renderstates FUN_00643430(0x800/8/0x10/4/0x4000,...), grey vertex colors from patch[+0x10/+0x11/+0x13] * -8 clamped 0..255. So: roof/shroud patches are tagged with high nibble 0x90/0xa0, associated to one of two per-sector "rooms", and the rooms byte in engine+0x92b4[...*0xd8] is the on/off switch flipped when the hero enters. SINGLE REMAINING GAP: the WRITER of engine+0x92b4 was not found - a scalar scan for 0x92b4 across all instructions returned nothing so the store site computes the base differently; bounded follow-up is to chase FUN_00417e70() (returns the engine/game singleton) and find writers into the 0xd8-stride array. SECOND RELATED LIST: when patch flags +0x1e & 0x10 AND nibble in {0x10,0x20,0x90,0xa0}, a rect is pushed to view+0x86888 - so 0x10/0x20 are the UNCONDITIONAL siblings of the conditional 0x90/0xa0. STATIC.PAK 64-BYTE RECORD (VERIFIED, in-memory record IS the file record; static = FUN_00635e50(patch[+0x04]), failure prints "StaticObjekt fehlt :%d"): +0x04 item-type id passed to FUN_00425ea0 returning PakItemType; +0x08 u32 flags read FOUR ways - (flags & 0x290)==0 REQUIRED TO DRAW AT ALL so bits 0x10/0x80/0x200 mean SKIP ENTIRELY; (flags & 0x800)==0 part of the selectable/marker push; (flags & 8) and (flags & 0x20) SELECT DIFFERENT DRAW BUCKETS (distinct vertex lists at view+0x96af8 etc). +0x0e and +0x12 i32 world X and Y subtracted from camera origin for screen pos - CONFIRMS our unaligned-i32 ox/oy measurement. +0x27 passed to FUN_00634150; +0x2b i16 compared ==1. ROW 662 FLAG HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: file layout confirmed but semantics are NOT what we guessed. VERIFIED 0x08 and 0x20 are RENDER-BUCKET SELECTORS, 0x10 is DO-NOT-RENDER, 0x00 is the default bucket. Nothing treats them as "building part" vs "ground clutter" - that may still correlate but the codes own meaning is draw-list routing, and 0x10 is a SUPPRESSION BIT not a "rare unique marker". BONUS VERIFIED: PakItemType.flags IS read - bits 0x4, 0x10000, 0x800000 tested on the FUN_00425ea0 record; 0x10000 combined with static[+0x08]&0x800==0 and static[+0x2b]==1 gates a push into view+0x96ae0 with tag 8. WLDXENTRY +0x0c IS A FLOOR.PAK HANDLE (VERIFIED behaviour, HYPOTHESIS on identity): if patch[+0x0c] != 0 the patchs 0x90-byte vertex block is copied into a SECOND list at view+0xb64+i*0x90 (cap 0x6d5 = 1749) and the +0x0c value itself stored in a parallel int array at view+0x3e3c4 - a handle drawn in a later overlay pass, NEVER used as a static.pak index. World loader FUN_00633ae0 @ 0x00633ae0 opens .\WORLD\STATIC.PAK -> cWorld+0x238 AND .\WORLD\FLOOR.PAK -> cWorld+0x23c side by side (prints "STATIC.PAK v%d #%d" and "FLOOR.PAK v%d #%d"), plus SECTORS.KEYX/SECTORS.WLDX (falling back to non-X .KEY/.WLD), .\PAK\TILES.PAK, .\WORLD\TRIGGERS.PAK, bin\World.bin. This RESOLVES the row 663 vs 662 +0x0c disagreement: it is a real sparsely-populated NON-static.pak handle and the reason 0 of 2145 resolved is that they were never meant to; monotonic-with-cell-index is consistent with a floor-pak authored in scan order. Matches Resacreds floorId naming. NOT CLOSED: the pass consuming view+0x3e3c4 was not read to confirm it indexes FLOOR.PAK directly. RESACRED HEADER CORRECTED (VERIFIED): patch +0x10..0x13 are the FOUR SIGNED CORNER HEIGHTS (subtracted from screen Y, scaled by 1/zoom) and +0x14..0x17 are the FOUR CORNER BRIGHTNESS BYTES (replicated into ARGB vertex colors). Resacreds rest[8] at 0x10 and smthX..W at 0x18 are OFF BY FOUR. +0x00 tileId indexes a 64-BYTE-STRIDE tile table where +0x20 is the texture id (bound via FUN_006292c0) and +0x24 is a u16 into a per-view 0x20-stride UV table.

column5: VERIFIED. Repo /tmp/smv = github.com/Qronikarz/sacred-minimap-viewer, 4 files, single commit 2021-10-02 by MrQuerter, MIT: readme.md, notes_and_javascript_generators.txt (the derivation in the authors working notes), minimap_view.html (816KB materialized table), demo_minimap_view.png. Parsed all img tags and checked every one: 10000 tiles, j and i each covering exactly 0..99, complete 100x100, ZERO formula violations. The mapping is a formula; the empiricism was only in DISCOVERING it. WHAT "not like normal puzzles" MEANS (VERIFIED by area arithmetic): lattice basis vectors are j+1 -> (+256,+128) and i+1 -> (-256,+128); fundamental cell area = |256*128 - (-256*128)| = 65536 = 256^2, so the 256x256 square images tile the plane EXACTLY, no overlap no gap - only possible if each TGA holds a DIAMOND of content with transparent interlocking corners. Standard 2:1 isometric stagger, nothing exotic. SECTOR MAPPING (VERIFIED): 100x100 minimap tiles <-> our 100x100 sector grid, 1 tile per sector, 256px per 64 cells = 4 px/cell in x and 2 px/cell in y. j behaves as gx, i as gy: screen-x prop (j-i), screen-y prop (i+j), 2:1 coefficient ratio 256:128 - EXACTLY the shape of our worldToScreen = [[2,-2],[1,1]]/sqrt(5). Independent confirmation of the transforms FORM and of axis roles (gx -> screen-SE, gy -> screen-SW). Filename order is {gx_sector}{gy_sector}, x first. HYPOTHESIS: transparent-corner diamond content means a minimap tile is a ROTATED sector, so sector->tile is a rotation not a crop. THE HEADLINE - ONE SOURCE NOT TWO: exact bbox of the assembly computed from parsed HTML - tile origins span x 0..50688, y 0..25344; full bbox with the 256px tile = 50944 x 25600. Tile-origin diamond corners vs the community maps STATED anchors: top apex (25344,0) vs (25608,0); left (0,12672) vs (0,12672); right (50688,12672) vs (51216,12672); bottom (25344,25344) vs (25608,25344). EVERY Y VALUE IS IDENTICAL: 0, 12672, 12672, 25344. And 12672 = 99*128, 25344 = 198*128 - pure artifacts of a 256px-tile / 128px-y-step / 100-tile assembly. A genuinely independent survey does NOT land on 99*128 to the pixel. VERIFIED: the community interactive maps coordinate frame IS the minimap assembly (or both descend from the same assembly of the same tile set). NOT independent corroboration. Row 658 cross-validation collapses to a single source. The x axis differs by exactly 97/96 = 1.0104166 (51216/50688 = 25608/25344): the community author fitted x with the last tile column INCLUDED (4.00125*6400 = 25608 ~= 25600 = 100 tiles x 256) but fitted y with the last tile row EXCLUDED - 1.98 = 2 * 99/100 EXACTLY, short by precisely one tile in a hundred, using max-tile-origin 25344 as the extent instead of 25344+256 = 25600. x coefficient 4.00125 vs true 4.0 is a 0.03% fudge. So the community transform is not merely non-independent, it is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: correct convention on x, off-by-one-tile on y. CORRECT TRANSFORM: mapX = 25600 + 4*(gx-gy), mapY = 2*(gx+gy). SILVER CREEK PIN (VERIFIED arithmetic): if the only error were the transform, true cell (3213,2502) would report at (3242,2531) = +29 both axes. Observed pin is (3188,2808). Transform explains ~29 cells of drift; the remaining ~277 cells of gy error is NOT transform error. HYPOTHESIS: the Silver Creek pin is a hand-placed POI that is simply wrong. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS. THE 50900x25235 README NUMBER IS JUNK (VERIFIED): aspect 2.01704 vs tile-origin diamond 50688/25344 = 2.00000 exact, full bbox 50944/25600 = 1.99, community 51216/25344 = 2.02083. The README number is 44px narrower and 365px SHORTER than the repos own generator produces, matches no geometric construction, and the 0.017 excess is NOT explained by overlap (there is none, the lattice tiles exactly), border, or rounding. HYPOTHESIS: an eyeballed/devtools render size from the authors failed screenshot attempt, soft to ~+/-400px. DO NOT USE 50900x25235 as a measurement of anything. The hard number is 50944 x 25600; the meaningful one is the tile-origin diamond 50688 x 25344 = exactly 2.000000, the trivially expected 2:1 iso diamond over a square world, carrying no information beyond "tiles are 256px and there are 100 of them".

column4: ROOF-CUTAWAY MECHANISM FOUND (writer-traced, unlike retracted row 667). It is NOT a geometric "player is inside" test and NOT per-region-family. It is a DATA-DRIVEN SPRITE-VARIANT SWAP keyed on a cTrigger runtime state word, in the static-object loop at the tail of FUN_0062ae90 (~0x62b960-0x62c250). THREE byte-identical skip sites, one per emission branch: 0x62bad0 (itemType flags&0x4), 0x62bd89 (itemType flags&0x800000), 0x62bef0 (static flags&0x8 = the building bucket). Each does: anchor=local_3e0; if(!anchor) no gating; EDX=anchor->triggerId(+0x27); ECX=world->triggerTable(+0x268); AX=PakStatic+0x2b (u16 VARIANT MASK); CMP AX,[EDX*0x10+ECX+0xa] (cTrigger.state); JNZ 0x62c246 = loop-advance, i.e. sprite never emitted. ANCHOR LOOKUP once per cell, guarded by floorcell+0x1e bit0: FUN_006354d0 = cWorld::getParentObject, CONFIRMED BY ITS OWN ERROR STRING at 0x0095fe4c "cWorld::getParentObject() Invalid State for Ref[0] State[0]"; it scans the cell static chain for the record with flags&0x10 and returns it. THEREFORE static.pak flag 0x10 is NOT merely do-not-render: it marks the BUILDING ANCHOR/ROOT, an invisible marker carrying the buildings triggerId at +0x27.

column4: CONFLICT RESOLVED: IT IS A SWAP, NOT A CULL. Row 671s cull-polarity inference is WRONG. Mechanism: each building is a PAR world object carrying MULTIPLE COMPLETE SPRITE SUBSTATES; the trigger bitmask selects WHICH SUBSTATE IS DRAWN. column4: ROOT CAUSE OF THE DEAD CUTAWAY TRIGGER FOUND AND FIXED: Sacred.Regions.cell_class collapsed the NON-ZERO class bytes 0xd0/0xe0 onto EMPTY. It read `return 0 if b == 0 else b & 0x0f`, so any byte whose class nibble is 0 came back indistinguishable from a raw 0x00 (uncovered) cell. 0xd0+0xe0 are 39,644 cells world-wide - more than double FLOOR's 16,302 - and they are the buildings' OPEN INTERIOR GROUND. Measured at the pinned Seraphim spawn: sector 50,39 carries exactly ONE region (anchor 3213,2502 size 34x30 family KLOSTER_KAPELLE01) whose rect DOES contain the spawn cell 3236,2511 at local 23,9, and that cell's raw byte is 0xd0. An ASCII dump of the whole 34x30 grid shows 0xd0 tiling the octagonal nave wall to wall and 0xe0 tiling the library wing beside it, with 0xd1 walls ringing both. So row 679's 'derive() resolves NO footprint at the hero's own cell' was HALF RIGHT: the footprint resolved fine, the CELL CLASS decoded to EMPTY, class_is_open said false, and _triggered() could never be true. FIX: cell_class now returns a new Sacred.Regions.OPEN (0x10, deliberately not a nibble value) for a non-zero byte whose nibble is 0, EMPTY only for a raw 0x00; Walkable.class_is_open gains OPEN; verify_ref.py's WALKABLE_CLASSES mirror gains 0x10.

column4: PAINTER-ORDER OVERLAP: BOTH PER-OBJECT SORT KEYS ARE WRONG, AND THE REAL FIX IS A LAYER FIELD WE HAVE NEVER READ. The defect measured exactly: sector_view.gd sorts objects by pos.y descending, where pos is the static's own iso SCREEN position (static.pak +0x0e/+0x12), so the key is the object's ANCHOR. A sprite is drawn DOWNWARD from origin.y = pos.y - spr.anchor.y, so a large composite and a small prop anchored on the same iso diagonal get near-identical keys while the composite's geometry reaches many cells further front. Concrete pair from OBJ_TRACE=50,39: KLOSTER_KAPELLE01_2_00D at cell (3225,2510), 460x719, pos.y -137661, and a bush at cell (3238,2497), 158x150, pos.y -137666 - the SAME diagonal, 3225+2510 == 3238+2497 == 5735 - so the bush sorts after the wall whose lower half it stands behind, and paints over the chapel's north wall. TESTED FIX, REJECTED: keying on the sprite's FRONT edge instead (pos.y - anchor.y - size.y; front edges -138380 vs -137816, which orders that pair correctly) does remove the bush overlap, and REGRESSES the interior - the big floor/wall composite now sorts LAST and paints over every bench, the altar and the candle stands (shot tmp/roofverify/r680/sort-fix.png against tree-fix.png). Reverted; after-revert2.png is byte-identical to tree-fix.png. Per-TILE sorting does not rescue it either: a bench stands ON the floor, so the floor tile beneath it always has the lower front edge and still wins.
column5: WHY NO PER-OBJECT KEY CAN WORK: the two cases demand opposite orders from the same pair of numbers. A composite must draw BEFORE the props standing on it (anchor key wins) and AFTER the props standing behind it (front-edge key wins). One scalar per object cannot express both, so this is not a sort-key bug to be tuned - it is a missing LAYER separation. Ground/floor art has to be a layer below object art, the way terrain already is.

Read of /tmp/opencode/resacred (LordSk/Resacred-old, HEAD 86cd6ec): it has NO sort (grep sort|qsort|std::sort over rs_game.cpp, rs_renderer.cpp, rs_resources.cpp = zero matches), NO depth test (`//glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);` COMMENTED OUT at rs_renderer.cpp:634, no glDepthFunc or glDepthMask anywhere), and writes literal z=0.0 for every quad (meshAddQuad call sites rs_game.cpp:393 statics, 406/421 tiles). It walks the sector's 4096 cells at rs_game.cpp:337-338 in flat index order i = y*64 + x and splats quads in that order; only one sector is ever drawn (sectorDrawData[0], rs_game.cpp:788). It is a map viewer that never had props and walls competing for occlusion. DECISIVE NEGATIVE: PakStatic.layer, PakItemType.flags and PakItemType.category are referenced in the ENTIRE codebase only as ImGui debug text (rs_game.cpp:682, 698, 738) - never branched on, never used to bucket or order. mixedId (rs_game.cpp:370) is the only PakItemType field real logic consumes. So the only public RE effort never found the ordering rule either, which corroborates row 685 rather than contradicting it.
column5: TWO USEFUL BY-PRODUCTS. (1) sacred_worldToScreen (rs_game.cpp:233-238) makes screen y = x*0.44721359 + y*0.44721359 - BOTH axes weighted equally, so screen depth is proportional to (worldX + worldY). Our own data agrees and this port is NOT miskeyed: the bush at cell (3238,2497) and the wall composite at (3225,2510) have pos.y -137666 and -137661, a difference of 5 in 137,000, and 3238+2497 == 3225+2510 == 5735. static.pak +0x0e/+0x12 really are already the iso screen position, as AGENTS.md says. (2) PakItemType is 128 bytes (rs_file.h:358-386) and its only named-but-never-read fields that smell spatial are marginX/marginY at +0x5d/+0x5f. Flagged as a lead, not a finding.
column6: LEAD FOR ROW 684, from the format's shape rather than from code: retail may sort the SUB-SPRITES, not the objects. A composite is a PakMixedDesc of PakMixedData entries each carrying its own md.x/md.y offset (rs_file.h:286-299), which Resacred emits as separate quads (rs_game.cpp:387-394) and simply never sorts. Sorting those individually would let a wall's lower sub-quads land in front of props while its upper ones stay behind - the one thing a per-object scalar provably cannot do (row 684). NOT YET TESTED. Note the earlier per-TILE objection still has to be answered: a bench stands ON the floor, so whether this works depends on keying each tile by its own screen ANCHOR rather than its bottom edge.

column4: world/triggers.pak IS DECODED AND IT IS THE WORLD'S DYNAMIC-OBJECT REGISTRY. Layout: magic TRG v1, u32 count @+4 = 2268, a fixed header at 0x100 of {136, 268, 36288} whose 268 is the data offset and whose 36288 == 2268*16, then 2268 sixteen-byte records at 0x10c; 0x10c + 2268*16 == 36556 == the exact file length, which is what fixes the stride. Record: +0x00 u32 trigger id (== record index for live records), +0x04 u16 kind (16 = live, 1246 records; 0 = dead/erased, 1022 all-zero records), +0x06 u32 static.pak RECORD INDEX = the back-link, +0x0a u16 always 1 for live, +0x0c u32 always 0. THE BACK-LINK IS BIDIRECTIONAL: static_pak[trigger[i].+0x06].+0x27 == i for 1246 of 1246 live triggers, 0 mismatches. WARNING: triggers.pak is NOT a generic Pak container despite its magic being in Sacred.Pak.ALLOWED_MAGIC - the bytes at 0x100 are a fixed header, not an index, so reading it through Sacred.Pak silently misreads it. The same warning applies to pak/creature.pak (CIF, 41020 B, count=474 @+4): its 0x100 index is garbage (offsets like 251989775); it is a FLAT table of (41020-256)/474 = 86.0000 exact stride.
column5: +0x08 == 0x10 IS THE DYNAMIC-OBJECT DISCRIMINATOR. Trigger ids rise monotonically with sector, so the table is spatially authored. Sector 50,39 contains exactly ONE trigger-carrying static out of 935: rec 758529, items rec 3489 'mage_elements_cowl.grn', sprite 0, 0 tiles, +0x08 0x10, trigger 2034, cell (3219,2511) in the chapel nave. Roster of the 1246 live triggers, 109 distinct target names: 490 unnamed (items records that are entirely zero, 144 distinct type ids in 734..4503 - INFERRED to be creatures defined in creature.pak instead), mage_elements_cowl.grn x92, mage_elements_legs.grn x87, MUMMY.GRN x36, FX_BOSSDEATH x24, FX_MAGICFADE x21, W03.GRN x19, S01.GRN x18, Hornisse02.grn x17, Hoellengolem01.grn x17, plus ~40 FX_* names. So one table holds monsters/NPCs, visual effects and creature-defined spawns. HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: the sector's zero-art statics are NOT NPC markers - there are 192 of them, all MiniObjTex* (types 1033/1035/1037/1053/1061/1062), every one with trigger 0 and +0x08 in {32,96}. column4: THE PRIESTESS PATH IS BLOCKED ON APPEARANCE, NOT ON PLACEMENT, AND FOUR LINK HYPOTHESES ARE NOW REFUTED. Placement is fully solved by row 690 and needs nothing further: sector 50,39 static rec 758529, +0x08 == 0x10, trigger 2034, cell (3219,2511), back-link verified both ways. What is NOT known is WHAT TO DRAW. (1) 'static items name -> the whole NPC mesh' REFUTED: models.pak resolves the name to index 631, but MAGE_ELEMENTS_* is a SIX-PIECE EQUIPMENT SET - ARMS 627, BELT 628, BODY 629, BOOTS 630, COWL 631, LEGS 632 - so the static names one garment, a cowl. items.pak carries the same six as separate records (arms 3449, belt 3461, body 3473, boots 3530, cowl 3496, legs 3508), all sprite 0. And characters are NOT assembled from six statics: the world-wide live-trigger roster has 92 cowls and 87 legs but ZERO arms, belt, body or boots. (2) 'PakItemType.spawnInfoId (+0x18) indexes creature.pak' REFUTED: it is 0 for all 1246 live triggers, one distinct value. (3) 'some remaining unknown static/items field carries a creature id' REFUTED by a field scan over all 1246 targets: no field has creature-scale cardinality with per-type stability. The only fields that are both non-constant and stable per item name are it+0x00 flags (10 distinct), it+0x04 (3), it+0x14 (12) and it+0x2e category (15) - none near creature.pak's 474. st+0x17 parentId is 1246-distinct, i.e. a per-instance id, not a type link. column4: pak/creature.pak IS DECODED, AND A CREATURE'S APPEARANCE NEEDS NO FIELD AT ALL - THE ID IS THE MODEL. Flat CIF table, 474 records of 86 bytes from offset 256; 256 + 474*86 == 41020 == the file length, which fixes the stride. THE DECISIVE FINDING: a creature's id at +0x00 IS an items.pak RECORD INDEX, and that record names the creature's Granny model. Two independent agreements establish it. (1) The period German table's hardcoded ids 1..9 are the nine playable heroes in a fixed order (Seraphim, Gladiator, Kampfmagier, Dunkelelf, Waldelfe, Vampirin, Vampirin Wandelform, Zwerg, Daemonin); items.pak records 1..9 name SERAPHIM.GRN, GLADIATOR.GRN, MAGICIAN.GRN, DARKELVE.GRN, ELVE_SORCERESS.GRN, VLADY_D.GRN, VLADY_N.GRN, dwarf.grn, Daemonia.grn in that same order - 9 of 9 match - and all nine carry class 1 (Held). (2) It generalises: 473 of 474 creature ids name an items record and ALL 473 of those name a .grn. This also EXPLAINS row 692's ambiguous 184-of-756 signal, which is now retracted as ambiguous: those 184 trigger targets ARE creatures, and their class histogram is a coherent monster population - Monster 102, Untoter 41, Daemon 19, Tier 11, Soeldner 9, NPC 2. The remaining 1062 are 490 unnamed and ~330 FX_* effect markers.
column5: FIELD TABLE, verified against retail bytes: +0x00 u32 id, +0x04 u16 class, +0x06 u8 flags, +0x07 u8 ?, +0x08 u16 xpA, +0x0a u16 xpB (exp = A + level*B), +0x0c..0x11 six base attributes (Staerke, Wiederstand, Geschick, physische Regeneration, mentale Regeneration, Charisma), +0x12 u16 always 0, +0x14..0x25 eighteen skill bytes, +0x26 u16 walk speed, +0x28 u16 run speed, +0x2a..0x35 six (bonus level, bonus type) pairs, +0x36..0x3b six bonus values. That is 60 of 86 bytes, matching the source table's own 'zu ca. 70% aufgeschluesselt' claim exactly. THE 26 UNDESCRIBED BYTES (+0x3c..0x55) ARE MEASURED NEAR-CONSTANT - 1 to 11 distinct values per byte across all 474 records, and no u16 window in them lands in models.pak range for more than 22 of 474 - so no model or equipment index lives there, which is consistent with the id already being the model. Class enum, all observed values inside it: 1 Held (9), 2 Monster (71), 3 NPC (82), 4 Pferd (11), 5 Untoter (49), 6 Tier (62), 7 Soeldner (39), 8 Goblinoide (15), 9 Daemon (32), 10 Drache (15), 11 Energiewesen (12), 12 Elf (13), 13 Feind (unused in retail), 14 Mensch (56), 15 Dryade (7), plus one record at class 0. SOURCE: Creature.pak.txt from SacredModdingStuff1.zip (sacred-tribute.com), used as a HYPOTHESIS to test, never as fact - every field above was checked against the bytes.

column4: THE UNREAD floor.pak LAYER IS LARGE AND SECTOR 50,39 WAS UNREPRESENTATIVE. world/floor.pak is 188 MB / 6,713,136 records and the port never opens it; WldxEntry +0x0c is its handle. Row 662 measured +0x0c as ZERO for all 4096 cells of sector 50,39 and that reading is correct but local. Sampled every 7th sector across the whole 100x100 grid (125 present sectors, 512,000 cells): 87,830 cells carry a NON-ZERO +0x0c, i.e. 17.2%, and the maximum handle seen is 6,713,135 == count-1, so the whole table is referenced. Hit counts per sampled sector run to 1270 (7,7), 1147 (7,14), 937 (21,14), 873 (28,14), 813 (35,14). So roughly one world cell in six points at content this port has never read.
column5: RECORD SHAPE, measured: 16 bytes, +0x00 = the record's own index (1,2,3,100,1000 read back as 1,2,3,100,1000), +0x04 = a large value with no obvious range (183430683, 172944907, 198110699, 155250164, 71388), +0x08 = 0, +0x0c = a NEXT INDEX that is either 0 or self+1 (1->2, 2->3, 1000->1001, 3->0, 100->0). That is exactly the XentaxWiki decode of the OBJ/type-135 record {File Index, Unknown, Tag_CDCDCDCD, Next File Index} except that +0x08 reads 0 here rather than 0xCDCDCDCD. CONSEQUENCE: floor.pak is CHAINED the same way static.pak is (row 686), so whatever it holds is a per-cell LIST, not a single item. The meaning of +0x04 is undecoded and is the whole question.
column6: PROBE: godot-port/floor_scope_probe.gd, read-only. Do NOT conclude from row 662 that +0x0c is dead - that was one sector. This is now the single largest unread thing in the retail data by volume.

column4: world/floor.pak +0x04 IS DECODED: ITS LOW 17 BITS ARE A tiles.pak INDEX, AND THE FILE IS A PER-CELL OVERLAY-TILE LAYER. The 16-byte record is +0x00 own index, +0x04 payload, +0x08 zero, +0x0c next index (0 or self+1), so a cell's WldxEntry +0x0c handle heads a CHAIN exactly like static.pak's nextStaticId (row 686). The split of +0x04 is 15/17, pinned from BOTH sides rather than eyeballed. Upper bound: tiles.pak holds 90,132 records, so a real 17-bit tile index must always land under 90,132 while an unrelated field would do so only 68.77% of the time - measured 6872 of 6872, and one bit wider (18) immediately drops to 70.2% against its own 34.4% chance. Lower bound: 2595+ of the sampled values EXCEED 65535 inside that field, which a 16-bit field could not hold, so the boundary is not 16. Then every referenced tile resolves exactly like a terrain tile: texture id inside texture.pak's 25,535 AND orientation inside 0..17, for all 6872, across 690 distinct textures. This CONFIRMS the 2006 XentaxWiki page's speculation that floor tiles are referenced by an index into Tiles.pak, with the correction that the index is 17 bits, not 16.
column5: THE TOP 15 BITS ARE NOT DECODED - do not guess. 417 distinct values, range 0..1535, value 0 by far the commonest (2595 of 6872), and hundreds of distinct values WITHIN a single sector (259 in 7,7 / 119 in 14,14 / 342 in 50,39), so it is not a sector id, and its most common adjacency delta pairs with the tile index's own (+0x20001 = high +1, low +1), so it is not obviously a layer or draw order either. TWO HYPOTHESES TESTED AND REFUTED ON THE WAY, DO NOT RETRY: (a) '+0x04 low 16 bits index items.pak' and (b) 'floor.pak is a creature/NPC spawn table'. The names looked overwhelming - WOLF.GRN x123, BAT.GRN x63, CROW.GRN, RABBIT.GRN, HARPIEN.GRN, FARMER_FEM.GRN, skel_warrior_03.grn - but a RANGE-MATCHED background killed it: computing the .grn and creature-id rates per 1024-wide bucket of items.pak index and weighting by the observed value distribution gives observed/expected of 0.89 for .grn on the low half, i.e. BELOW chance, and the high half scored HIGHER on creature membership (2.17) than the low half (1.46). Raw set membership is worthless on this file because creature ids cluster low and .grn items cluster in bands.
column6: CHECK: new godot-port/floor_check.gd asserts the 6,713,136 count, the self-index and 0-or-self+1 chain shape, all sampled low-17 values under 90,132, all of them resolving to a valid texture id and orientation, the >=65536 lower-bound discriminator, and that an 18-bit read is visibly worse. PROBES: floor_scope_probe, floor_field_probe, floor_fit_probe, floor_id_probe, floor_spawn_probe, floor_stat_probe, floor_tile_probe, floor_resolve_probe, all read-only. NOTE for anyone extending this: tiles.pak does NOT open through Sacred.Pak (its ISO index is record data) - use Sacred.Tiles, which takes a PATH, not a Pak.

column4: ROW 695 MISSTATES ONE NUMBER: it says '2595+ of the sampled values EXCEED 65535' inside floor.pak +0x04's low 17 bits. That figure was carried over by mistake from a DIFFERENT measurement (the hi16-names control in the refuted spawn-table test) and is wrong. The measured value is 530 of 6872, i.e. 7.7%. Caught by floor_check.gd itself, whose lower-bound assertion had been written against the wrong number and fired on a clean run.
column5: THE DECODE IS UNAFFECTED AND THE LOWER-BOUND ARGUMENT STILL HOLDS. What the test needs logically is that the field holds ANY value at or above 65536, because a 16-bit field cannot hold one - and a 16-bit mask measures exactly 0, which is what the red-check produced. 530 is comfortably that. The rate is low simply because low tile ids are commoner than high ones: tiles 65536..90131 are only 27% of tiles.pak's 90,132 records. Everything else in row 695 stands and was measured, in particular 6872 of 6872 under 90,132 against a 68.77% chance rate, the 70.2% collapse at an 18-bit read, and full resolution of every referenced tile to a valid texture id and orientation.
column6: Threshold in godot-port/floor_check.gd corrected from n/10 to a flat floor of 100, with the real 7.7% rate written into the comment so the next reader does not re-derive it. LESSON, and it is a process one: two background jobs were left mutating and reading floor_check.gd at the same time, which raced and made a failed restore look like a passing run. One job per file.

column4: bin/TYPE_NPC_*/DefPos.bin IS DECODED: IT IS THE TABLE OF NAMED WORLD POSITIONS - quest markers, NPC spawn points, teleport sources and targets - one file per playable class. Row 689 identified the file and guessed 216 x 2777 from the raw size; that factoring was WRONG. Measured layout for type_npc_seraphim (599,832 B): a 12-byte header {u32 1234, u32 1908, u32 0}, then 5998 records of 100 BYTES, then 20 tail bytes. The stride was fixed by the ASCII names, which land at file offsets 12, 112, 212, 312 ... exactly 100 apart. Record: +0x00 name NUL-padded (longest observed 30 chars), +0x40 u32 world cell X, +0x44 u32 world cell Y, +0x48/+0x4c 0xFFFFFFFF on every record seen, +0x0c 4 / +0x18 22 / +0x50 22 / +0x54 4096 constant. 3463 of 5998 records hold an in-world cell (below 6400 in both axes), spread over 850 distinct sectors, range (0,0)..(6323,6328).
column5: IT NAMES THE CHAPEL'S OCCUPANTS. Within 40 cells of the pinned Seraphim start (3236,2511): pos_seratelehier30 at (3238,2513) and pos_seratelehier309 at (3237,2512) - 'sera tele hier', the arrival marker, two cells from the spawn; novizin1 at (3239,2525) INSIDE the chapel footprint 3213..3246 x 2502..2531, the female novice who is almost certainly the priestess of the oracle plate; POS_AUFTRAG_15001 at (3216,2513) (Auftrag = quest) also inside it; POS_ZIEL_15001 (Ziel = target) at (3252,2546); pos_novizen1_0..5_0 scattered 3223..3246 x 2528..2546; togo10 at (3238,2520); Tutorial_Kaempfen4 at (3200,2531). So the priestess IS authored in a file we can read, by NAME and CELL.
column6: WHAT IT DOES NOT SOLVE, stated plainly so nobody over-reads this: DefPos.bin carries NO creature id and NO model reference. It answers WHERE and WHAT IT IS CALLED, not WHAT TO DRAW. The name->appearance link must live in the script bytecode beside it - the same directory holds funkcode.bin (3.8 MB), startcode.bin (562 KB), vectoren.bin (2.1 MB), questcode.bin (40 B) and questpoolcode.bin (0 B), none of them read by anything yet. Also note the file is a DUMPED IN-MEMORY STRUCT ARRAY: +0x10, +0x14 and +0x1c hold pointer-shaped values (0x00A184A8, 0x00BBA568) and the +0x28 field rises by exactly 26 per record. Those are dead addresses from the authoring machine, not data - do not try to decode them. CHECK: godot-port/defpos_check.gd pins the header, the 100-byte stride via the name field, the coordinate range, and the two chapel anchors by name.

column4: WldxEntry +0x18..0x1b ARE NOT THE OVERLAY-TILE BLEND. Prediction was written down before measuring: if the third per-corner byte array is the per-corner alpha of the floor.pak overlay tile a cell carries (row 695), then cells WITH a floor handle should show non-zero corner bytes far more often than cells without. Measured over 221,184 cells (every 11th sector across the grid): P(c3 | floor handle) = 0.2009, P(c3 | no floor handle) = 0.0761, lift 2.64. That is a real but WEAK association, and the joint counts kill it outright: 30,764 cells carry a floor handle with ALL FOUR corner bytes zero, and 13,907 cells carry non-zero corner bytes with NO floor handle at all. A per-corner blend for the overlay would be near-total in both directions. HYPOTHESIS REFUTED - do not retry it.
column5: WHAT THE SAMPLE DOES SAY, as characterisation rather than meaning: the values are SMALL AND SIGNED. Top values are 1 x19595, 2 x11598, 255 x8952, 3 x6516, 4 x3256, 252 x2836, 254 x2688, 5 x1398, 253 x1188, 6 x744 - i.e. roughly -4..+6 read as signed bytes, 20 distinct in this sample against row 218's 99 over a larger one, and 90.2% of cells have all four zero (row 218 said 91%, agreeing). That shape is a small signed per-corner DELTA, structurally like the +0x10 height field rather than like the +0x14 light field, which is never zero and steps by -20. Baseline for anyone continuing: 17.4% of cells carry a floor handle, 9.8% carry a non-zero third-array corner.
column6: NEXT STEP IS A RENDER EXPERIMENT, AND IT IS BLOCKED ON THE OVERLAY LAYER. Height and light were both settled by rendering them and looking, not by staring at histograms, and this field is now characterised as far as statistics can take it. Drawing floor.pak's overlay tiles first gives the oracle for both this field and floor.pak's own undecoded top 15 bits (row 695), so those two questions should be attacked together, in that order. PROBE: godot-port/corner3_probe.gd, read-only.

column4: THE floor.pak OVERLAY LAYER IS NOW DRAWN. row 695 decoded it and row 699 stalled waiting for it; this is that render. SectorView._tile_stack walks each cell's WldxEntry +0x0c chain in world/floor.pak (16-byte record: own index, payload, zero, next=0-or-self+1), takes the LOW 17 BITS of +0x04 as a tiles.pak index, and emits one more diamond per link into the SAME sector mesh, same 18-slot atlas UVs, same per-corner heights (+0x10) and lights (+0x14) as the ground tile under it. No second material and no alpha blending: the quad is pushed DEPTH_STEP*0.1 nearer the camera per stack level and terrain.gdshader's existing 'discard when alpha < 0.25' does the cutout, which is exactly what an overlay needs.
column5: MEASURED EFFECT: --region=50,50,1 goes from 28672 quads to 35340 over 7 sectors, i.e. 6668 overlay quads, ~953 per sector against the 17.2% cell rate of row 694 (696/4096) - the excess is chains longer than one link. Texture count is UNCHANGED at 63, so overlay tiles reuse the pages the ground already loads. Pixels, chapel sector 50,39 at zoom 900, before/after: bare grass gains scrub and gravel, the hard-edged tan road tiles gain stone paving that reads as a path rather than a stamped rectangle, cliff bases gain vegetation. This is a DECAL layer, and its absence is the blocky terrain the port has had since the beginning.
column6: TOP 15 BITS STILL NOT DECODED and deliberately ignored by the renderer - if they turn out to be draw order or blend, _tile_stack is the one function that changes. Chain walk is capped at OVERLAY_MAX=8 links, a guess with no measurement behind it, and refuses any next link that is not self+1 so a bad read cannot walk the 6.7M-record table. GATE MOVED: AGENTS.md's load-path invariant was '28672 quads, 63 textures' and is now 35340; both mentions updated. The row-699 corner3 question (WldxEntry +0x18..0x1b) is now unblocked - it named this render as its oracle.

column4: world/floor.pak +0x04's TOP 15 BITS ARE A SECOND tiles.pak INDEX - the field is TWO TILE IDS IN ONE u32, and the overlay is a TWO-TEXTURE BLEND. Found in the retail reader at 0x080e4ca5 (sacred_orig, .text 0x08053828 / file 0xb828), which splits the payload exactly as row 695 said - ecx = v & 0x1ffff, esi = v >> 0x11 - and then treats BOTH halves identically: edi is loaded with 0x12 and each half is divided by 18 for its diamond slot (0x080e4dbb, 0x080e4dc7), each is pushed into the SAME tile lookup against cWorld+0x254 (0x080e4de2, 0x080e4dfa), and the two results are written into ONE vertex struct as two UV pairs - low field to +0x00/+0x04/+0x20/+0x24, top field to +0x08/+0x0c/+0x28/+0x2c. A zero top field takes the single-texture path at 0x080e4cca instead; a nonzero one under the other mode byte sets a defer flag at 0x080e4d98, so retail renders these in two passes.
column5: CONFIRMED AGAINST THE DATA, not just read off the disassembly. Over 135,921 nonzero top values sampled at stride 31: every one is a valid tiles.pak index (135921/135921), and tiles.pak's own orientation field equals index % 18 for every one of them - the engine's derivation and the port's stored field are the same rule.
