That scan looked for the disp32 byte pattern and found six sites; an instruction-level sweep of the whole .text in IDA finds ELEVEN, because `lea eax,[edi+255h]` and `add eax,255h` forms are invisible to a naive byte search of memory operands only. The extra sites are a fourth creator (opcode 73's handler, at 0x082b4ac6 in sacred_orig, using the identical `if (v > 0) obj->+0x255 = v` idiom as CreateNPC), the read side of the serialiser, and one FALSE POSITIVE worth naming: sub_815B774 computes `base + 597` but it is an index-to-offset accessor over 3-byte-strided entries on a DIFFERENT object (its neighbours are 570, 573, ... 594, 597, 600), so the same number there means nothing. The conclusion stands after the wider sweep: four writers, one reader, one serialiser, and no comparison of the value's size.

column4: THE SPAWN TABLES ARE READ BY THE GODOT PORT, AND THE CHECK CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS ON ITS FIRST RUN. Added Sacred.Funk to godot-port/sacred.gd - a sibling data class in the established RefCounted style, no Resource, no autoload - plus godot-port/spawn_check.gd, the one runnable check (`godot --headless --path godot-port --script spawn_check.gd`, 0.58 s, PASSES: 5309 rolls / 2854 wildlife / 2455 hostile / 14000 entries / 22762 groups / 11498 sector records, every id in creature.pak). The reader walks funkcode.bin by the u16 length field, which needs no tag table at all, and only decodes bodies for opcodes 51/115/100; an unrecognised tag inside one of those is a hard error rather than a silent skip, precisely because unlisted tags are zero-width no-ops in the engine and would absorb a cursor error invisibly. Funk.pick() implements the weighted roll against the record's ACTUAL weight total, not a hardcoded 100, since only 74% of records sum to 100.
column5: TWO CORRECTIONS TO ROWS 728-730, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING THE CHECK RATHER THAN BY RE-READING THE DATA. First, RETRACTED: hostile (tag 0x36 = 310) records do NOT carry exactly four weighted entries. The entry-count histogram is 1:59, 2:414, 3:557, 4:1425 for hostiles and 1:1724, 2:132, 3:238, 4:760 for wildlife - the earlier claim read a median as a rule. The real discriminator between the two populations is the PRESENCE of the 0x34/0x33 fields, 2455 of 2455 hostile records and 0 of 2854 wildlife records, so the reader records presence as a flag because both halves are legitimately zero in some records. Second, INCOMPLETE: opcode 115 uses more tags than the dominant signature showed - besides 0x02 (57342) and 0x87/0x88/0x89 (22762 each) it carries 0x8b (7444), 0x1d (3212) and the STRING tags 0x67 (4306) and 0x1e (108). Omitting them shifted the cursor and the first GDScript run failed on tag 0x8b, which is the failure mode the check was written to produce.
column6: WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, AND WHY THE PORT DOES NOT SPAWN ANYTHING YET. Placement is not in these records: opcode 100 writes into whatever object sits at the engine's CURRENT SECTOR (globals 0x879a080/0x879a084 << 6), and all 39,569 spawn records in the file sit under a SINGLE script label, so which group applies where comes from script EXECUTION, not from the table. Emulating that means interpreting the Region%dInit / Sector%d%3.3dInit entry points named in startcode.bin, which is a separate job. Nothing was added to main.gd for the same reason the project already has integration debt around creature.pak and triggers.pak: a consumer that cannot draw a creature (GRN skeletal animation is halted, phase 5) would be dead code. verify.gd still passes unchanged (layer files=13 violations=0).

column4: PLACEMENT IS SOLVED: vectoren.bin IS THE PROCEDURE TABLE AND EVERY SPAWN RECORD SITS IN A NAMED SECTOR PROCEDURE. Format, read off the file: u32 count, padding to 88, then 84-byte records of a 64-byte name field and five i32 of which the first two are a BYTE OFFSET into funkcode.bin and a LENGTH. Consecutive entries tile the file - entry 0 is (0, 410), entry 1 is (410, 76) - which is what identifies the pair, and row 712's 'the 84-byte stride does not divide the file exactly' is explained: the 23,494 records end at 0x1e1d50 and 199,016 bytes of tail follow. 11,414 of the procedures are named Sector<n>{Init,Enter,Exit}, and attributing every opcode 51/100/115 record to the procedure whose range contains it places 39,476 of them in 5,684 distinct grid sectors with ZERO orphans. 2,453 sectors carry a hostile roll. The chapel sector (50,39) carries none, which is what a town sector should look like.
column5: THE COORDINATE ORDER IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND SO IS THE EXISTENCE OF A SECOND NAME FORM. sprintf("Sector%d%3.3d%s", x, y, phase) at 0x082a087a writes its two arguments into globals 0x879a080 and 0x879a084 on the very next two instructions - the same pair opcode 100's handler shifts left by 6 to build a world position - so the first field is gx and the trailing three digits are gy. The format alone cannot settle the order, so it was pinned against the world: read this way, 5,659 of 5,684 script sectors exist in sectors.keyx's real 6,050-sector set; read the other way, only 4,013. SECOND FORM, and it is a trap: the engine ALSO carries "Sector%dInit" at 0x086eb1b1, formatted from a single number at 0x081c5c3b next to Region%dInit - the dungeon path. 48 procedures use it, all with exactly two digits, and 93 spawn records live in 25 of them. A grid name can never be shorter than four digits (%d gives at least one, %3.3d always three), so length discriminates; these are kept with sector.x == -1 and the id in sector.y rather than force-fitted onto the grid.
column6: WIRED AND CHECKED, AND THE FIRST TWO RUNS BOTH FAILED IN USEFUL WAYS. Sacred.Funk now takes a bin/TYPE_NPC_* DIRECTORY, reads vectoren.bin, and attributes records with a moving cursor (records are walked in offset order and the procedures tile the file, so no binary search is needed); rolls_for(gx, gy) returns a sector's rolls. spawn_check.gd asserts zero orphans, 5,684 sectors, 5,659 real, 2,453 hostile, 93 dungeon-form records and an empty chapel; it passes in 0.78 s and verify.gd is unaffected. The failures worth recording: the FIRST run disagreed with the Python reference by 17 sectors, and the cause was that BOTH sides were fabricating coordinates for the two-digit names - Python padded left and invented sector (0,84), GDScript padded right and invented (84,84) - so the disagreement, not either number, is what exposed the second name form. The reference counts in rows 728-731 that were derived before this fix (5,709 sectors, 2,455 hostile sectors) are superseded by 5,684 and 2,453.

column4: THE ARMALION DEBUG BUILD YIELDS THE SCRIPT LANGUAGE ITSELF, INCLUDING ITS SOURCE FORM - BUT IT DOES NOT NAME +0x255. Three artifacts, all new. (1) Scripts/*.txt in the 2001 tree is the script language AS SOURCE, 3054 lines of it, with a register-machine calling convention: `asm movi 1, 4; creature_setLevel (-1, -1)` sets register 1 then calls, so the literal call arguments are placeholders and the real operands are the preceding asm moves. (2) The full function API is registered at runtime by sub_4C6E80, one block per function: strcpy the NAME into a slot, store the HANDLER (a /INCREMENTAL jump thunk), then argc and a flag, with the function's ID in [ebp+var_4] just before the name push. 62 of roughly 75 entries extracted to analysis/armalion-script-api.tsv - id, name, argc, flag, thunk, resolved body. (3) DEBUG.LOG in the same directory is a REAL RUNTIME TRACE of the 2001 engine: it opens with a sizeof table for 21 engine classes (cWorld 132448, cObject 64, cCreatureInfo 76, cEvent_creature 52, cGrnMdlChunk 1200) and then logs `sid[N] func[name] size[bytes]` per compiled script function - the direct ancestor of the vectoren.bin procedure table decoded in row 732.
column5: THE ID SPACES DO NOT MAP, SO THE ROSETTA STONE IS SEMANTIC, NOT NUMERIC. 2001 ids: item_createOnPatch 26, creature_setBehaviour 38, setAlliance 47, setGroup 48, setLeader 49, setLevel 52, morph 51, onPatch_creature 54. 2004 opcodes at those numbers are unrelated - 51 is the spawn roll, 54 shares a handler with 15, 26 is a label. Renaming 2004 opcodes from 2001 ids would therefore be pure invention and is not done. What DOES transfer is architecture: the 2001 setters never poke creature fields, they build an event with sub_401E1A and dispatch it through the creature's vtable slot 3 - event 6 for setLeader, event 266 for setAlliance - which is the same shape as retail's cEvent_creature(0x100) found in row 730. And the 2001 API has group, leader and alliance as THREE separate per-creature notions, which is suggestive next to retail's quartet of adjacent serialised i32 at +0x249 (the group id the alert sweep looks up), +0x24d, +0x251 and +0x255.
column6: WHAT THE ORACLE COULD NOT DO, STATED PLAINLY. The 98 `cClass::method(` debug strings in armalion.exe were dumped and searched: not one mentions a group, alert, alarm, alliance or leader FIELD, so the naming oracle of RESEARCH section 9.2 does not reach this question. The quartet reading {group, leader, alliance, X} is a HYPOTHESIS from the 2001 API's shape, not a fact, and +0x255 remains what row 730 measured it to be: a value written by four creators, read once as `> 0`, serialised with three neighbours, and never compared for magnitude. Mechanical notes for the next attempt: the repo's armalion.exe.i64 is NOT WRITABLE by the agent (idat fails with `Permission denied -> Database initialization failed with error 4`), so copy the exe and the .i64 to /tmp and open the copy; and ida_struct no longer exists in IDA 9, which kills any script that imports it.

column4: THE {group, leader, alliance, X} READING IS ONE CONFIRMED, ONE REFUTED, TWO UNDER-DETERMINED - AND THE TEST PRODUCED A BETTER FIND THAN THE HYPOTHESIS. Method: sweep every instruction in .text whose memory operand displacement is one of 0x249/0x24d/0x251/0x255/0x259, group by enclosing function, and read the functions that touch TWO OR MORE of them (51 functions touch the quartet at all, 21 touch two or more). CONFIRMED, +0x249 IS THE GROUP ID: the creature creator (sub_824F354, 0x0824f354) takes the group as a parameter, calls sub_82C296C(world, group, self_ref, 1) to REGISTER the creature in that group's member list, and only then stores it at +585; the alert sweep of row 730 looks that same list up by the same key. REFUTED, THERE IS NO PER-CREATURE ALLIANCE FIELD: the engine's same-side test is sub_819AABA(a, b), 154 bytes, and when its two cheap checks fail it falls through to an EXTERNAL relationship table, sub_83A004C(table, a.ref, b.ref) - alliance is a pairwise lookup, not a scalar on the creature.
column5: WHAT +0x24d AND +0x251 ACTUALLY ARE, AS FAR AS THE EVIDENCE GOES. Both are creature REFERENCES, not attributes: both are initialised to 0xffffffff in several places (43 write sites for +0x24d, 16 for +0x251), which is the engine's no-ref sentinel. +0x251 is the one sub_819AABA tests FIRST - `b->+0x251 == a.ref` returns same-side immediately - so it is an owner/master link pointing at another creature, and sub_8184456 additionally uses it as an object-manager key when its value is in 1..16, the same 1..16 window that gates the `Creature unregisterd in Sector(%d,%d)` path. +0x24d is written inside cCreature's event handler as `self->+0x24d = event->+5` immediately alongside `self->+0x259 = event->+2`, and the pair is then shipped together to a network call as (self_ref, +0x24d, +0x259) - that reads as the SOURCE and KIND of the last event, not as a leader link. So 'leader' is not established for either; what is established is that the quartet is group id, two refs, and the alert-response enable.
column6: METHOD NOTES. The 2001 API's group/leader/alliance triple was the reason to look, and it was worth looking - but a same-NAME triple in a four-year-older engine is a prompt, not evidence, and two of the three did not survive contact with the retail code. Two mechanical notes for the next sweep: IDA's operand-level scan found the READ sites cleanly but reported ZERO writers for both offsets, because a `mov [reg+disp32], reg` destination did not match the operand test I used; objdump over the same range found 43 and 16 writers immediately, so cross-check any 'no writers' result with a second tool before believing it. And the whole sweep runs against analysis/lgp-2010/sacred-1.0.02-final.i64, whose field offsets agree with install/sacred_orig even though the two builds are not byte-identical.

column4: THE ALLIANCE MECHANISM IS TWO SEPARATE TABLES, AND THE SECOND ONE IS A 16x16 CREATURE-CLASS FRIEND/FOE MATRIX SHIPPED IN .rodata AT 0x086f84e0. sub_83A004C, the function row 734 reached, is the PLAYER TEAM check and nothing else: it resolves each ref, and for a ref above 16 whose creature carries bit 2 at +0x1f4 it SUBSTITUTES THE OWNER REF FROM +0x251 (independent confirmation that +0x251 is an owner/master link, since a summon or a mount inherits its owner's side), then requires both values to land in 1..16 and compares team[a] == team[b] != 0. The table is a 76-byte object built lazily by sub_839DAAA (singleton at dword_8BB45FC), read by sub_839DB4A as `*(u32 *)(table + 4*slot - 4) & 0x7fffffff` -- so 16 u32 slots with bit 31 reserved as a flag. It is multiplayer: the same singleton is used by the function holding UI_NET_TEAM%d, UI_NETINFO_TEAMLEADER and UI_NET_INFO. Monsters therefore have NO team at all - for them this branch always returns 0.
column5: THE CLASS MATRIX IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR SINGLE PLAYER, AND IT DECODES CLEANLY AGAINST THE CLASS ENUM OF ROW 693. The constructor's second act is memcpy(byte_87994C0, &unk_86F84E0, 0x100) -- 256 bytes of .rodata copied into .data - and sub_83A0174 indexes it as byte_87994C0[16 * A->[+0x1f0] + B->[+0x1f0]], i.e. by the CREATURE CLASS. Reading the shipped matrix with the 15-class enum gives a table that is immediately recognisable: Held is hostile to Monster, Untoter, Goblinoide, Daemon, Drache, Energiewesen, Elf, Mensch and Dryade, and friendly to NPC, Pferd, Tier and Soeldner; TIER IS HOSTILE TO NOTHING except class 13, which is exactly the wildlife/hostile split the spawn tables show (row 729's type 100 population is class Tier); and class 13 Feind, which row 693 called 'unused in retail', has an ALL-ZERO ROW AND COLUMN INCLUDING ITS OWN DIAGONAL - hostile to everything including itself. That is a strong independent confirmation of the enum.
column6: TWO QUIRKS WORTH KEEPING. First, the matrix is NOT SYMMETRIC: 11 of the 120 pairs disagree, and NINE of them involve PFERD - the horse treats undead, goblinoids, demons, dragons, energy beings, elves, humans and dryads as hostile while every one of those treats the horse as friendly, which is exactly the behaviour a mount needs (enemies ignore the horse and attack the rider). The remaining two are Untoter/Dryade and Goblinoide/Dryade. Second, and this looks like a shipped bug: sub_83A0174 tests `M[b][a] == (M[a][b] ^ 1)` and, when that holds, RESTORES THE WHOLE MATRIX from .rodata - a self-repair for a matrix that lives in mutable .data. But the shipped default already fails that test for all 11 asymmetric pairs, so for any encounter involving a horse the restore fires every time and copies the same 256 bytes back over themselves. Harmless, but it means the check cannot be doing what it was written to do.

column4: THE CLASS MATRIX IS IN THE PORT, AND IT IS LOCATED BY ITS OWN SHAPE RATHER THAN BY AN OFFSET. Sacred.Factions in godot-port/sacred.gd reads the 16x16 friend/foe table of row 735 from the ENGINE BINARY under the configured install path - the table is 256 bytes of .rodata, not a data file, so there is nothing else to read it from and nothing is bundled. A hardcoded offset would have been wrong: the three builds tested do NOT agree on where it sits (install/sacred and the lgp-2010 binary at 0x6b04e0, install/sacred_orig at 0x6b7180). The search instead matches the table's own signature - a 16-byte-aligned window of nothing but 0 and 1 whose class-13 row is entirely zero INCLUDING its diagonal cell while every other diagonal cell is 1 - and that matches EXACTLY ONE window in each of the three binaries. The check runs in 0.39 s, so scanning 8.7 MB from GDScript needs no index or cache.
column5: THE CHECK ASSERTS THE THINGS THAT MAKE THE WINDOW UNMISTAKABLE, NOT MERELY THAT ONE WAS FOUND. godot-port/factions_check.gd verifies four independent facts, each of which agrees with a finding recovered by a different route: Feind (class 13) is hostile to every class including itself, which is what row 693 meant by calling it unused; Tier is hostile to nothing but Feind, which is exactly the wildlife population of the spawn tables (row 729's tag 0x36 == 100 group); the hero's enemy list is Monster, Untoter, Goblinoide, Daemon, Drache, Energiewesen, Elf, Feind, Mensch, Dryade and no one else; and the matrix has 11 asymmetric pairs of which 9 involve Pferd. That last one is asserted deliberately - a future edit that 'fixes' the matrix into a symmetric table would be a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, since the asymmetry is what makes enemies ignore a mount and attack its rider.
column6: STATE. Three checks now pass side by side: factions_check (matrix at sacred+0x6b04e0), spawn_check (5309 rolls placed in 5684 sectors, all ids in creature.pak) and verify.gd (layer files=13 violations=0). Nothing consumes the matrix yet and that is stated in the class comment rather than hidden: creatures cannot be drawn until GRN skeletal animation is solved, so the rule is parked in one place for when they can. The natural first consumer is not rendering at all - it is the spawn tables, since a sector's rolls plus each creature's class plus this matrix is enough to answer what would actually fight what in any given sector, with no renderer involved.

column4: THE THREE SYSTEMS ARE JOINED AND THE JOIN ANSWERS A GAMEPLAY QUESTION WITH NO RENDERER INVOLVED. Added Sacred.Creatures to godot-port/sacred.gd - the missing reader for pak/creature.pak, exposing only the two fields the join needs, the id at +0x00 and the class at +0x04 - so the whole join is one expression: factions.hostile(HELD, creatures.class_of(id)). godot-port/spawn_factions_check.gd walks all 14,000 weighted spawn entries, asserts that EVERY id resolves to a creature.pak class in 1..15 (join integrity - this is what breaks first if either reader drifts), and reports per sector what would actually fight the hero. Runs in 0.64 s. All four checks now pass side by side: spawn_factions_check, factions_check (matrix at sacred+0x6b04e0), spawn_check (5309 rolls in 5684 sectors) and verify.gd (layer files=13 violations=0).
column5: THE JOIN CORRECTS HOW ROWS 729 AND 736 DESCRIBED THE TWO POPULATIONS: TAG 0x36 IS NOT A HOSTILITY SPLIT. Measured over every entry, it has exceptions in BOTH directions. The 0x36 == 100 population is 5610 Tier and 132 UNTOTER, so a 'wildlife' roll can put hero-hostile creatures on the map. The 0x36 == 310 population spans twelve classes and only 7051 of its 8258 entries are classes the hero fights - the remaining 1207 are Soeldner (607), Tier (594) and even Pferd (6), all of them hero-FRIENDLY. So 0x36 selects a population, and hostility is a separate question answered by the class matrix; the earlier shorthand of wildlife-versus-hostiles was a good first approximation and is now bounded by numbers.
column6: AND THE 132 UNDEAD IN THE WILDLIFE POPULATION ARE COWS. They are ids 524, 526 and 528, 44 rolls each, and all three name COW.GRN through items.pak - every cow in the game carries creature.pak class 5, Untoter, which the shipped matrix turns into hostile-to-the-hero. It reads like a data slip and it is NOT to be fixed: canonical-first is the project rule, so the check asserts the undead cows are still there (`the wildlife population lost its undead`) rather than filtering them out. If a later tuning layer wants cows to be Tier, that is an explicit opt-in mod, not a silent correction in a reader.

column4: THE SPAWN JOIN IS NOW VISIBLE: --spawns TINTS EACH SECTOR BY WHAT ITS ROLLS WOULD PUT ON THE MAP. Green = wildlife only, amber = a hostile roll containing nothing the hero fights, red = a hostile roll the hero fights, untinted = the sector rolls nothing at all - which is what a town sector like the Silver Creek chapel (50,39) looks like. 2,738 of the world's 6,050 sectors are tinted. The tiers are computed ONCE in main.gd._spawn_tiers() using the same one-line join the check uses - Funk says what a sector rolls, Creatures turns each id into a class, Factions says whether the hero fights that class - and handed to SectorView as plain data, so the view still opens no file of its own. _build_spawns paints cell-by-cell like the existing --flags1e and --classhi overlays rather than inventing a second piece of iso projection maths for one big diamond.
column5: VERIFIED BY LOOKING, WHICH IS THE ONLY ORACLE THAT COUNTS FOR A RENDERER. `sh analysis/tools/look.sh port --spawns --region=51,17,2 --noplayer` renders sector 51,17 - the busiest spawn sector, 12 rolled entries of which 4 are hero-hostile - as a solid red diamond with green wildlife-only neighbours and untinted sectors between them, terrain still legible through the tint at alpha 0.30-0.38. The default path is unaffected: a plain `look.sh port` still renders, and all four checks still pass (spawn_check 5309 rolls in 5684 sectors, factions_check matrix at sacred+0x6b04e0, spawn_factions_check join clean over 14000 entries, verify.gd layer files=13 violations=0). The Funk parse only happens when the flag is passed, so the startup cost is opt-in.
column6: WHAT THE PICTURE IS AND IS NOT. It shows where the scripts WOULD roll, not what the retail engine actually has standing there at any moment: opcode 51 is a weighted roll executed at sector entry, the count comes from the 0x35 range, and nothing here executes it. So a red sector means 'the tables here can produce something hostile to the hero', not 'N monsters are placed at these coordinates'. Per-creature placement does not exist in the tables at all - it is produced at runtime by the roll plus the engine's own position search - so the overlay is deliberately per-SECTOR and no finer.

column4: THE THREE REFUTED RIG-AGREEMENT VERDICTS MEASURED THE WRONG QUANTITY, AND THE RIGHT ONE SEPARATES 78% vs 4%. Rows 605/606/609 each composed WORLD bind transforms and each came back REFUTED. Compared LOCALLY -- each bone's own rest transform, chain never composed -- the SAME two files agree: GLAD_ATTACK_1H_A.GRN vs GLADIATOR.GRN (model 589) matches 60 bones by name, of which 47 agree within 0.01 and max error is 6.737522; the wrong-character control BATX_ATTACK_BH_A.GRN against the same model manages 1 of 26 and max 43.550049. THE CORROBORATION THAT MATTERS: 47/60 and 6.737522 are, to the digit, planning_measurements' own pre-stated expectation which row 609 recorded and could NOT reproduce -- reached here from a differently-motivated test, not aimed at. column6: CONSEQUENCE, and the rule any future edit must not break: bind a clip to a mesh BY NAME onto the MODEL's hierarchy and apply the clip's keys as LOCAL transforms; never compose the clip's own chain, never treat the clip's rest as a bind pose. This is what ModelView.play_clip already did, which is why reader-level playback worked (row 610) while the rig premise read as refuted. godot-port/rig_check.gd is the ONE runnable check and fails if someone 'improves' the binder into composing world transforms. CORPUS GENERALISATION, honest limits stated: an UNFILTERED search of ___GARG_FLY_ATTACK.GRN against all 1572 meshes -- no name filter at any step -- returns GARGOYLE.GRN at 0.973 over 74 bones, and across a 118-clip sample every clip's top-1 mesh scores 0.79..0.97 over 46..80 bones. I did NOT put an identification-accuracy number on this: there is no ground-truth clip->character map, and my own 3-letter-prefix scorer reported 0.3136 while its 'misses' were correct (DDRU->DRYADDRUID, DUEL->DUNKELELVE, HORS->BRIDLE_01, ICEE/ICEC->DARKELVE, BRID->BLACK_RIDER) -- the prefix rule is the broken instrument, not the geometry. BEARING ON A WITHDRAWN REQUIREMENT, flagged not acted on: R1.4 (one shared skeleton across equipment-slot meshes) was WITHDRAWN by human decision row 613 on the strength of rows 605/606, which used the world-space quantity this row shows to be the wrong one. Several equipment meshes of a character score 0.86..0.91 against that character's clips locally. Whether that reopens R1.4 is a human call, not taken here.

column4: CREATURES NOW STAND IN THE WORLD AND ANIMATE, AND THE CLIP FOR EACH ONE IS CHOSEN BY BONE GEOMETRY BECAUSE THE NAMES DO NOT LINE UP. Sacred.Rigs (godot-port/sacred.gd) maps a mesh entry to the clip whose bones agree with it, using row 739's local-rest comparison and no name filtering at all. It has to: a clip is called UPI1_WALK_BH.GRN while its mesh is UPIRATE_01.GRN, DDRU_IDLE_BH.GRN belongs to DRYADDRUID.GRN, HORS_DYING_A.GRN goes with BRIDLE_01.GRN. Over the 124 distinct meshes the spawn tables name, a four-letter prefix rule resolves 41; Rigs resolves 121, scores 0.844..1.000, and refuses the other 3 rather than animate a creature with another creature's skeleton (MIN_SCORE 0.5, measured spread real 0.79..0.97 vs wrong-character 0.04).
column5: MEASURED. godot-port/rigs_check.gd is the ONE runnable check and runs the real work load, not a sample: every spawn id -> Items.name_of -> Models.index_of -> Rigs.clip_for. 14000 spawn entries -> 124 distinct meshes -> 121 clips resolved (97.6%), scores 0.844..1.000. The id->mesh half of that chain is 251/251 exact -- every creature id the spawn tables name resolves to a models.pak entry, via items.pak +0x37 (row 693's 'the id IS the model'). Cost is one 7-second pass over all 3397 clips, cached to user://rigmap.tsv keyed by the models.pak byte size: 15091 ms cold, 0 ms warm, nothing bundled and nothing written beside the retail data. Spot checks are named rather than aggregate so a human can see a wrong answer: BEAR.GRN must pick a BEAR* clip and WOLF.GRN a WOLF* clip.
column6: WIRING, and what it is NOT. --creatures draws the spawn tables in the player's own sector: Funk.rolls_for -> pick() honouring the weights -> Items.name_of -> PlayerView (now taking a model name; default unchanged, so every existing call site is untouched) -> ModelView.play_clip, each rig seeked to a random phase so a sector of wolves does not breathe in lockstep. First live run, --spawn=2896,2896 (sector 45,45): rolls=3 built=3 animated=3, gob_warrior.grn x1 and RABBIT.GRN x2. THE CEILING, named rather than implied by the picture: placement is a deterministic scatter around the player under a fixed seed, NOT retail placement -- retail rolls spawn points at runtime from data this port does not read yet. They stand and animate; there is no wandering, no AI, no despawn, and no creature actor in the sim. The default monastery spawn sector (45,51) legitimately rolls nothing, so --creatures there correctly draws nothing and says so. VERIFIED BY LOOKING, per this project's rule that a renderer claim needs a frame. `sh analysis/tools/look.sh port --creatures --spawn=2896,2896`. Creatures-vs-control pixel diff: 2004 of 746496 pixels differ, bbox (556,49)-(636,497), and the amplified diff resolves into TWO clearly bipedal silhouettes at different depths -- not a stack at the model origin, which is what a failed placement would have produced. MOTION verified separately, because a posed frame and an animated one look identical in a single capture: added --shot-delay=SECONDS (main.gd, the port had NO way to capture a non-settled frame before, so no animation had ever been shown in a capture) and diffed t=0 against t=1.5s -- 618 pixels differ, confined to the SAME creature bbox with the rest of the frame byte-identical, and the outline is recognisably a rabbit's ears and a goblin's arms. The rigs render very dark, like the player's own rig; that is pre-existing and untouched here. REGRESSION: verify.gd 13 files 0 violations, plus rig_check, rigs_check, factions_check, spawn_check and spawn_factions_check all pass.

column4: R1.4 IS REOPENED AND CONFIRMED: A CHARACTER'S EQUIPMENT MESHES DO SHARE ITS SKELETON, MEASURED LOCALLY. Human decision 2026-08-14 ('reopen R1.4 with the local measurement'), superseding the withdrawal in row 613 -- which was itself a human decision taken on rows 605/606, both WORLD-SPACE measurements, the quantity row 739 showed to be the wrong one for this shape of question. Re-measured with the local instrument (each bone's own rest transform, chain NEVER composed, matched by exact bone NAME) over 6 character families and 301 rigged equipment pieces: median own-base agreement 0.9661 against median cross-character 0.0196, a 49x separation, and median TOPOLOGY agreement 1.0000 -- every name-matched bone has the same named parent on the piece as on the base. Per-family own/cross: GLAD 0.8246/0.0189, SERA 0.9123/0.2059, AMAZ 0.2059/0.1471, DARK 0.9841/0.0189, DWAR 0.9661/0.0192, MAGE 0.9859/0.0556.
column5: MEASURED, with the verdict rule fixed BEFORE the first run and not adjusted after: CONFIRMED iff median own > 0.8 AND median own > 5x median cross; anything else REFUTED. godot-port/equip_check.gd is the ONE runnable check and asserts the verdict, so a later edit that re-refutes R1.4 fails loudly rather than silently. The cross-character control is the load-bearing half and is what rows 605/606 lacked: the SAME pieces measured against a DIFFERENT character's base, rotating through the family list so every control is a real character. A piece sharing too few names with the control base scores 0.0 rather than being dropped, so the strongest disagreements stay in the control's median instead of being quietly removed. Pieces carrying no rig of their own (25 of 326) are counted and reported, never folded away.
column6: THE ONE DISSENTING FAMILY, diagnosed and NOT fixed to improve the score. AMAZ measures 0.2059 own against 0.1471 cross -- no separation. Cause: the AMAZ wardrobe SHIPS TWICE. Entries 17-25 carry AMAZONE_ARMOUR_KROTENHAUT/KURZKHEMD/LHARNISCH/TUCH/CLOTH/LEATHER/METAL at ~70 bones, entries 380-388 carry the SAME NINE NAMES at ~62 bones, and AMAZONE.GRN (entry 379) has 76. The prefix grouping therefore merges two rig generations into one family and measures half the pieces against the wrong base. This is the conservative-instrument caveat written into the check before it ran -- a wrongly-swept piece can only LOWER a family's agreement, never inflate it -- so AMAZ understates R1.4 rather than contradicting it, and the pieces agree with EACH OTHER at frac=1.000. The family table was left as measured; the verdict was already CONFIRMED without it and re-grouping after an unfavourable sub-result is the re-scoring this project refuses (05-10 precedent). SEPARATE CAVEAT, honest and unresolved: a shared rig is NOT unique to one character -- AMAZONE_HELMET_LEATHER.GRN agrees 1.000 with SERAPHIM_HELM_LEATHER_01.GRN. Skeleton identity constrains WHICH rig a piece binds to, not WHICH character wears it. WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it licenses drawing base + equipment pieces on one shared pose (they share names, topology and local rests, so one pose drives all of them). It does NOT establish which pieces retail actually composes for a given equipped item -- that mapping is unread, and phase 05's 'whether retail composes equipment visually' remains the parked research question row 613 named.

column4: --equip= DRAWS A BODY AND ITS ARMOUR AS SEPARATE MESHES ON ONE SHARED POSE, WHICH IS R1.4 MADE VISIBLE. `--equip=GLADIATOR.GRN,GLAD_SA5` builds 7 meshes (body + ARM/BELT/BODY/HELM/SHOES/SHOULDER), hands every one of them the SAME clip through the SAME unmodified ModelView.play_clip, seeks them all to the same time, and the result reads as one armoured figure mid-stride: horned helm on the head, pauldrons on the shoulders, bracers on the arms, boots on the feet. There is NO retargeting step and no per-piece binding code anywhere in the path -- the pieces stay on the body only because they genuinely share its skeleton (row 741). The clip was not named by hand either: Sacred.Rigs picked GLAD_WALK_BH.GRN from bone geometry, so the picker (row 740) is exercised end to end by the same command.
column5: VERIFIED BY LOOKING. /tmp/look/port-102945.png via `sh analysis/tools/look.sh port --equip=GLADIATOR.GRN,GLAD_SA5`. equip line: meshes=7 built=7 animated=7 clip=GLAD_WALK_BH.GRN verts=2483 tris=3281. The set is named explicitly rather than inferred, because 'GLAD' alone matches 80 meshes -- every armour variant the Gladiator owns -- and overlaying all of them is not an outfit; --equip= takes a comma-separated prefix list so the caller says which set. EQUIP_SEEK=0.35 poses mid-clip rather than at rest on purpose: in the bind pose a still frame cannot tell a shared skeleton from a coincidence.
column6: THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WEAKER THAN THE POSITIVE, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN DRESSED UP. Cross-family pieces do NOT fly off the body: `--equip=GLADIATOR.GRN,SERAPHIM_METAL --anim=GLAD_WALK_BH.GRN` (port-103247.png) still deforms the Seraphim armour with the Gladiator's walk, because both are Biped rigs sharing most bone NAMES -- the pieces sit wrong (clipping through the torso, floating shards at chest and hip, a stray piece behind the head) rather than detaching. So the visual difference between a right and a wrong set is 'armour that fits' vs 'armour that does not', not presence vs absence; the rigorous control for R1.4 remains the numeric one in equip_check.gd (own 0.9661 vs cross 0.0196 over 301 pieces), not this picture. TWO EARLIER CONTROL ATTEMPTS WERE CONFOUNDED and are recorded as such, not as evidence: SERAPHIM_HELM on the Gladiator half-passes because helmets are small rigs shared ACROSS characters (row 741 already measured AMAZONE_HELMET_LEATHER agreeing 1.000 with SERAPHIM_HELM_LEATHER_01), and `--equip=AMAZONE.GRN,GLAD_SA5` is confounded three ways at once -- AMAZONE.GRN has no decodable mesh, Rigs therefore picked a Dryad clip for it, and the camera framed on an arm. TWO BUGS IN THE DEMO ITSELF, found by looking and fixed: _show_equip never awaited _maybe_screenshot so a capture run hung instead of failing, and the camera was framed on entry 0 unconditionally, so one undecodable mesh at the head of the list captured a blank grey frame.

column4: THE EQUIPPED-ARMOUR -> MESH MAPPING IS bin/rust.bin, AND IT IS KEYED BY THE WEARER'S BODY MESH. Layout, fixed by exact arithmetic: u32 count = 85 at +0x00, then 85 GROUPS, each u32 n followed by n PAIRS of u32 (wearer_body, armour_mesh) -- both members are items.pak RECORD INDICES, and an items.pak record's +0x37 name is a .GRN filename (row 693's 'the id IS the model' chain, reused unchanged). The parse consumes 1098 of 1098 u32s exactly, yields 85 groups and 506 pairs, and 506 of 506 pairs have BOTH sides naming a mesh -- 100%, which is what fixes the layout. One group is one equippable armour item; its pairs say which mesh to draw on each wearer. Group 40 is the clearest read: DARKELVE.GRN->DElve_s_arms.grn, ELVE_SORCERESS.GRN->elve_s_arms.grn, GLADIATOR.GRN->GLAD_s_arms.grn, MAGICIAN.GRN->MAGE_s_arms.grn, SERAPHIM.GRN->sera_s_arms.grn.
column5: MEASURED, and corroborated by the engine's own strings. 13 distinct wearers appear in the left column: DARKELVE 77 entries, VLADY_D 71, ELVE_SORCERESS 70, SERAPHIM 70, MAGICIAN 53, GLADIATOR 51, THIEF2_FEM 24, THIEF2_MAL 21, AMAZONE 18, ORC_WARRIOR 16, OGRE_CLOTH 15, gob_warrior 11, BARBARIAN 9 -- the playable classes plus the humanoid NPCs that wear armour. The 85 groups are ordered by SLOT and MATERIAL and read as a catalogue: 0-16 and 75-84 body armour (Tuch/Kurzhemd/Krotenhaut/Leather 01-03/Metal 01-02), 17-21 helmets, 22-38 amulets (AM_ = Amulett: Brosche, Feuer, Knochen, Totenkopf, Luft, Mond, Sonne, Spiral, Stern, Wasser, Erde, each with an _ed 'edel' variant), 39-44 s_arms, 45-50 s_belt, 51-56 s_boots, 57-62 s_legs, 63-68 s_shoulder (six quality tiers per slot, all sharing one mesh, which is why GLAD_s_arms.grn appears 6 times), 69-74 gloves. PROVENANCE FROM THE BINARY: install/sacred carries 'scripts\\Rustungenswitch.txt', 'bin\\Rust.bin' and 'compiling %s' adjacent in .rodata with the parser keywords new/Item/set/end, so Rust.bin is COMPILED from a Rustungenswitch.txt ('Ruestungen switch' = armours switch) that retail does not ship; the same string block shows scripts\\sets.txt -> bin\\sets.bin and scripts\\waffenmod.txt -> bin\\wpmod.bin, plus the item-modifier vocabulary (PD/FD/MD/GD, ASpeed, MinLev, MinRare, Rare: EINS/ZWEI/DREI/VIER). The 2001 Armalion tree does NOT contain Rustungenswitch.txt -- checked, it predates the system.
column6: WHAT IS STILL OPEN, stated rather than papered over: the group index 0..84 is the armour item's identity, but WHAT SELECTS IT is NOT established -- no field in an inventory item has been shown to carry it, and I did not find the referencing side. So the port can answer 'given this armour type and this wearer, which mesh' but not yet 'given this dropped item, which armour type'. SECOND OPEN ITEM: the numbered set meshes (GLAD_SA5_*, items records 1986-1990 and 3017) are ABSENT from rust.bin, and bin/addon/ contains no second armour table (only merc.bin). A scan of every bin/*.bin for those ids reports hits in world.bin, wpmod.bin, static10_18.bin and the engine itself, but these are NOT claimed as references: 1986..1990 are ordinary small integers and a 4-byte match inside a 45 KB file is far likelier coincidence than a pointer. bin/sets.bin is a DIFFERENT table and not a mesh mapping -- it parses exactly as u32 count=66 then 66 records of 28 u32 (1 + 66*28 == 1849 == the file's u32 count), whose columns 0-9 hold a variable-length member list (occupancy 65,65,65,60,52,41,19,8,2,1), columns 10-11 two further fields and 12-27 zero padding; its members are item ids, only some of which name meshes. wea.bin does NOT parse under rust.bin's layout and is left undecoded.

column4: NOTHING CARRIES A 0..84 INDEX, BECAUSE rust.bin IS NOT INDEXED - IT IS A SWITCH TABLE KEYED BY THE ARMOUR MESH ITSELF. This CORRECTS row 743's closing framing, which called the group ordinal 'the armour item's identity' and named finding its referencing side as the open question. There is no referencing side. The runtime operation is: take the armour mesh an item carries (an items.pak record index) -> find the group containing it -> read the pair whose WEARER is the current character -> draw that mesh. The source filename says so and I read past it the first time: Rustungen-SWITCH.txt. Verified end to end: GLAD_s_boots.grn worn by MAGICIAN.GRN -> magician_boots.grn (group 51); gladiator_am_mond.grn worn by VLADY_D.GRN -> vlady_AM_Mond.grn (group 29); AMAZONE_LEATHER.GRN worn by SERAPHIM.GRN -> Seraphim_leather_04.grn (group 2).
column5: MEASURED, four independent agreements. (1) UNIQUENESS: 503 distinct armour meshes across 506 pairs, and only 3 appear in more than one group -- so the mesh alone identifies a group for 500 of 503. (2) THE LEFT COLUMN IS NOT PART OF THE KEY: distinct (wearer, mesh) pairs == 503 == distinct meshes, i.e. every mesh always pairs with the same wearer, so the wearer is a FUNCTION of the mesh and the left column merely declares whose version a mesh is. (3) NO INDEX EXISTS TO FIND: a column scan of all 32768 items.pak records over every u8 and u16 field offset 0x00..0x36 found no column reaching 84 with 85 distinct values (best candidates: +0x21 max=76 distinct=20, +0x2e max=33 distinct=27), and no bin/*.bin file contains all 85 values (wpmod.bin 62 of 85, balance.bin 66, world2.bin 13). (4) items.pak is NOT an item catalogue at all: of 17408 named records, 2859 are .grn meshes and 14549 are world objects (Pavillon01, TH11 Innenwand u 1_03, DungeonA49_a), so there is no equippable-item record to hang an index on.
column6: HONEST LIMITS, and a METHOD NOTE worth more than the finding. LIMITS: the 3 ambiguous meshes are the cloth entries (AMAZONE_CLOTH and ELVE_MAGICAN_CLOTH in groups 0 and 1, ELVE_SORCESS_CLOTH in groups 0 and 5), an authoring duplication; 8 of 85 groups list one wearer TWICE, so a (group, wearer) lookup can return two meshes (DARKELVE.GRN -> both DarkElve_Metal_01.grn and elve_metal_01.grn in group 82) and a consumer must pick or refuse; and not every wearer has a variant in every group -- Gladiator_Metal_01.grn worn by SERAPHIM.GRN returns nothing, which is a real class restriction, not a decode failure. METHOD NOTE: STRING-BASED XREF HUNTING DOES NOT WORK ON THIS BINARY. install/sacred contains the literals 'bin\\Rust.bin', 'bin\\sets.bin' and 'bin\\wea.bin' but ZERO 4-byte references to any of their addresses, and the literals models.pak / creature.pak / items.pak / balance.bin / vectoren.bin / funkcode.bin DO NOT APPEAR IN THE BINARY AT ALL -- filenames are built inline with immediate stores (the same idiom visible at file offset 0x30fb4e, which assembles 'Armbrust' as 'Armb' + 'rust' + NUL and is what a naive grep for 'rust' finds first). Future work should reach for the data-shape route before the xref route on this target. world2.bin was examined and DISCARDED as a lead, not decoded: it is [u32 32768][32768 bytes] but every nonzero byte value occurs exactly 280 times, which is a generated pattern rather than a per-record table.

column4: THE SWITCH IS WIRED INTO --equip, AND WIRING IT CORRECTED ROW 744 TWICE. Sacred.Armour (godot-port/sacred.gd) reads bin/rust.bin and answers 'what does this armour become on that wearer'; --equip= now treats its FIRST prefix as the wearer and switches every other mesh, so a Gladiator's gear list pointed at a Darkelve comes back as Darkelve gear. Verified by looking: `--equip=DARKELVE.GRN,GLAD_s_arms,GLAD_s_boots,GLAD_s_legs,Gladiator_Metal_01,Gladiator_helmet_metal` prints switched=5 and draws a long-haired, pointed-eared Darkelve in spiked plate mid-stride (/tmp/look/port-110348.png), built from DELVE_S_ARMS/DELVE_S_BOOTS/DELVE_S_LEGS/DARKELVE_METAL_01 -- five meshes, one pose, no retargeting. Applying the switch unconditionally is safe because a wearer's own mesh switches to ITSELF, which armour_check pins.
column5: MEASURED. godot-port/armour_check.gd is the ONE runnable check: 85 groups, 506 pairs, 8 duplicate-wearer groups, and BOTH keyings pinned -- ambiguous by items.pak RECORD 3, by FILENAME 109 of 284 distinct names. CORRECTION 1 TO ROW 744, which said 'only 3 appear in more than one group, so the mesh alone identifies a group for 500 of 503': that is true of the RECORD and false of the NAME. 503 armour records spell only 284 distinct .GRN filenames, so ~219 records are the SAME mesh file registered again as a different armour, and 109 filenames span several groups -- for 74 of them the group choice CHANGES the answer for some wearer. The items.pak RECORD is the item identity; the filename is not. This matters because a caller holding a models.pak entry has only the filename, so Armour exposes variants_for_record() as exact and variants_for() as a documented best-effort union with is_ambiguous()/group_count() alongside, and --equip prints every ambiguous substitution rather than picking in silence.
column6: CORRECTION 2, retracting a claim rows 743/744 made twice: 'Gladiator_Metal_01.grn worn by SERAPHIM returns nothing, a real class restriction' IS WRONG. It was an artefact of first-group-wins. That filename is TWO armour records: the one in group 82 lists no Seraphim, the one in group 9 lists Seraphim_metal_01.grn. Both statements are true of different armours that share a mesh file; neither is a class restriction. armour_check assertion 3 now pins exactly this case so the wrong reading cannot be re-derived. METHOD NOTE, paid for twice today: A FAILED assert() IN A SceneTree CHECK SCRIPT HANGS INSTEAD OF FAILING -- the script halts but the tree keeps running, so the run sits until its timeout with EMPTY output and looks like a slow decode. The first armour_check run burned 280 s that way and the misleading symptom sent me looking at Items.new (measured: 35 ms, not the cause). Every check script in godot-port/ has this hazard. SEPARATE, NOT A SWITCH FAILURE: DARKELVE_HELMET_METAL.GRN has no decodable mesh, so the helmet is skipped and 5 of 6 meshes build; that is a ModelView decode gap, unrelated to rust.bin. Regression: verify.gd 13 files 0 violations.

column4: A FAILING CHECK NOW FAILS INSTEAD OF HANGING. godot-port/check.gd is a shared SceneTree base for all 21 check scripts; every check now `extends "res://check.gd"`, calls super() as the first line of its _init, and exits through finish(code) instead of quit(code). The base connects process_frame in its _init: since every check completes inside _init, reaching the FIRST PROCESSED FRAME means _init never reached an exit -- i.e. it aborted -- so the failsafe prints why and quits 1. Proved on a disposable script that asserts false: exit=1 in under a second with the assertion text visible, against exit=124 after the caller's full timeout with EMPTY output before the change.
column5: MEASURED, and two mechanisms were tried and rejected on evidence before this one. (1) OVERRIDING SceneTree.quit() so existing call sites would mark themselves automatically -- IMPOSSIBLE HERE: `The method "quit()" overrides a method from native class "SceneTree" ... (Warning treated as error.)` is a hard compile failure under this project's settings. (2) RELYING ON THE BASE _init RUNNING AUTOMATICALLY -- FALSE: measured with a two-script probe, GDScript does NOT call a base _init when the child defines its own, so without an explicit super() the failsafe is never armed and the hang returns unchanged. column5: A LATENT RECORD/REPLAY DIVERGENCE WAS FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY, AND IT WAS OLDER THAN THIS CHANGE. Fixed by recording what the live run actually applied (one value per advance, computed from the same expression the live path uses), so record == live by construction. column5: THE VERDICT IS REFUTED AND IT IS MY RULE'S FAULT, NOT THE DATA'S, AND I AM NOT FLIPPING IT AFTER THE FACT. I wrote the local pass's discrimination rule as a mechanical copy of the world-space shape -- control must match strictly FEWER names AND agree strictly LESS AND have a strictly LARGER max. Clauses 1 and 2 pass decisively (25 < 60/61; 0.0400 < 0.9167/0.9180). Clause 3 fails: the control's maxlocal 39.566605 is SMALLER than either helmet's 71.689812 / 74.358704. That is an artefact of sample size, not of agreement -- the control matches 25 bones where the helmets match 60 and 61, so it has fewer opportunities to contain an outlier, and `max` reports the worst single bone rather than how well the rig agrees. Changing the rule now, having seen it fail, is the re-scoring this project refuses (05-10 precedent), so the printed verdict stands as measured and the check still exits 1.
column6: THE CORRECTION IS A HUMAN CALL AND IS NOT SELF-AUTHORIZED, BUT IT IS NOT POST-HOC REASONING ABOUT THE DATA EITHER: the two-clause form -- control matches fewer names AND agrees less -- is ALREADY the established rule in this codebase. rig_check.gd separates on the within-fraction with a 10x ratio and no max clause; equip_check.gd separates on median own > 0.80 and own > 5x cross, again with no max clause. The clause required the control's maxlocal to exceed each helmet's. Measured: control 39.566605 against helmets 71.689812 and 74.358704 -- the control's worst bone is CLOSER, not further. That is sample size, not agreement: the control matches 25 bones where the helmets match 60 and 61, so it has fewer opportunities to contain an outlier, and `max` reports one bone rather than how well a rig agrees. The surviving two clauses separate decisively on the same data -- 25 < 60/61 matched, and 0.0400 against 0.9167/0.9180 within. maxlocal is still measured and still printed on every fact line; it simply no longer decides.
column6: NOT AN INVENTION TO MAKE THIS PASS: the two-clause form is what this codebase already uses everywhere else the same question is asked -- rig_check.gd separates on the within-fraction with a 10x ratio, equip_check.gd on median own > 0.80 and own > 5x cross, neither carrying a max clause. The three-clause version was the novelty. FULL SUITE STATE: 21 scripts, all exit 0. This is the first time the whole check suite has been green in this session; it began the day with door_transition_check failing (rows 747-748, an 08-13 self-contradiction between row 631's trigger corridor and the check's own exterior destination), swap_walk failing (rows 749-754, a pre-door-teleport route later rebuilt to walk in and out of OZELT3 at 53,28,0), the AGENTS.md layer-1 parity gate structurally unable to pass (row 748, tiles.pak), and every check silently HANGING instead of failing on a bad assert (row 746).

column4: CREATURES ARE NOW LIT IN THE STREAMED WORLD, AND THE CAUSE OF THEIR BLACKNESS WAS A MISSING LIGHT, NOT A MATERIAL BUG. Everything SectorView draws is SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED -- the retail art is already lit -- while ModelView builds the one LIT StandardMaterial3D in the scene. In the world path ModelView is constructed with frame_camera=false, which suppresses the camera AND the key light it would otherwise add, so every rig was a lit surface with no light in the scene: near-black silhouettes that a pixel diff could find and an eye could not. Fixed with main.gd _ensure_rig_light(), a single DirectionalLight3D added ONLY when a rig is actually built, using ModelView.LIGHT_DIR and a new shared ModelView.KEY_ENERGY (1.5, promoted from a literal so the world and the --grn= preview light a creature identically).
column5: MEASURED, and it corrected my own eyeball. The lit capture at sector 45,45 LOOKED brighter overall than the pre-light one, which would have meant the light was touching terrain and would have put every frame-md5 gate at risk. Pixel diff says otherwise: 781 of 746496 pixels differ, 0.1%, bbox (556,49)-(636,497) -- exactly the creature bounding box, zero terrain pixels moved. Unshaded materials ignore the light as claimed. No Environment was added on purpose: ambient would need a WorldEnvironment whose background mode repaints the area outside the map, and swap_walk/follow_parity assert frame md5s; a key light alone cannot touch a pixel no lit material covers. The unlit side of a rig therefore stays dark, which is ModelView's own documented trade-off when it has no fill.
column6: OPEN, AND NOT DIAGNOSED -- HANDED OVER RATHER THAN GUESSED AT. Captured in the open at sector 51,17 (--spawn=3296,1120 --zoom=1) the creatures are now visible but read as THIN, with stray fine geometry trailing above each figure. The mesh itself is NOT at fault: the same entry rendered through the model viewer (`--grn=Waldelfe_dark.grn`, index 404, verts 1656 tris 1792, bones count=90 roots=1 binds=69) is a clean, solid, correctly-proportioned figure. So the defect is in the WORLD path, and the obvious suspect is PlayerView baking placement into the ROOT BONE pose -- set_bone_pose_scale and set_bone_pose_position on every parentless bone -- while play_clip drives the same skeleton; the player has never exercised that combination because PlayerView has no clip. This is stated as a suspect, NOT a finding: the world view is a distant isometric shot of a deliberately slim model, so 'thin' alone is not proof, and the stray geometry above the figures is the part that actually needs measuring. Next step is a controlled comparison of the same creature built with and without play_clip.

column4: CONFIRMED, AND ROW 757's SUSPECT IS THE CAUSE: play_clip IS WHAT BREAKS A CREATURE MESH IN THE WORLD PATH. Controlled pair, one variable, same three rigs at the same cells in sector 51,17 (--spawn=3296,1120 --zoom=1): with animation the figures are visibly mangled -- splayed, stretched, stray limbs pointing off-body; with --creatures-noanim (new flag, builds the identical rig and skips ONLY the play_clip call, animated=0 in the log) the same meshes render as coherent upright humanoids. 4130 pixels differ between the pair, bbox (411,50)-(711,541), which is the three creature positions and nothing else. The mesh and the reader are exonerated independently: WALDELFE_DARK.GRN through the model viewer is a clean solid figure, verts 1656 tris 1792 bones 90 roots 1 binds 69 (row 757).
column5: THE MECHANISM IS NOT YET PINNED, ONLY THE TRIGGER. PlayerView places a rig by baking into the SKELETON's parentless bones -- set_bone_pose_scale(root, ONE * _scale) and set_bone_pose_position(root, rest * _scale + local_offset) -- and it does that because SectorView's depth sort reads each MeshInstance3D's global position as the sort key baseline, so the node itself must stay at identity (player_view.gd's own class doc). ModelView.build_animation writes per-bone LOCAL tracks and deliberately skips the CLIP's root (parent_effective == -1). Those two are not obviously compatible: the placement scale on the model's root propagates to every child while the animation supplies child positions in unscaled units, and the model root and clip root are not the same node (row 609: model 589 carries an alignment bone the clip has no node for). Which of those actually produces the splay is UNMEASURED and is deliberately not guessed at here.
column6: WHY THE PLAYER NEVER SHOWED THIS: PlayerView has no play_clip call and never has -- row 610 records that the PlayerView/streaming wiring was parked -- so the world path has only ever posed a STATIC skeleton for placement until --creatures started animating one. THE FIX DIRECTION, stated as options rather than a decision: either place the rig somewhere the animation cannot overwrite (a parent Node3D, which needs SectorView's sort-key baseline reworked because it currently requires identity global transforms) or re-apply placement AFTER the AnimationMixer writes each frame (Godot 4's SkeletonModifier3D is the sanctioned hook for exactly this ordering). --creatures-noanim is kept as the control that makes this measurable again after any attempted fix.

column4: THE SkeletonModifier3D APPROACH DID NOT FIX THE SPLAYED CREATURE RIGS, AND ROW 758's PROPOSED MECHANISM IS REFUTED. Implemented godot-port/view/rig_placement.gd, a SkeletonModifier3D that re-applies PlayerView's placement to the parentless bones inside the skeleton's modification phase -- i.e. AFTER the AnimationMixer writes each frame -- with PlayerView.update() reduced to feeding it a local offset. Three-way capture at the same cells in sector 51,17 (animated-broken / static / animated-with-modifier): the modifier panel is indistinguishable from the broken one, while the static panel remains the only coherent figure. So the distortion is NOT the placement and the animation fighting over the root bones; the ANIMATED POSE ITSELF is wrong, and re-ordering the writes cannot help.
column5: A SEPARATE REAL BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY, and it is worth more than the failed hypothesis: A NEW class_name IS NOT VISIBLE TO A `--path` RUN. rig_placement.gd first shipped with `class_name RigPlacement`, and player_view.gd failed to compile with `Identifier "RigPlacement" not declared in the current scope` because Godot's script-class cache is not refreshed for a brand-new global class in a --path run. The failure did NOT present as a compile error at the surface: the consumer silently failed to build, the capture never settled, and the run sat spinning with an EMPTY log until its timeout -- diagnosed only by running gate 2, which still printed 35340 quads / 63 textures while emitting the parse error. Fixed by dropping class_name and preloading by path, the same shape the check scripts use with "res://check.gd". Any future file added to godot-port/view/ should preload rather than rely on class_name.
column6: WHAT THE NEXT MEASUREMENT SHOULD BE, since this one refuted its own hypothesis. The model-viewer capture that exonerated the mesh (row 757, WALDELFE_DARK.GRN clean and solid) was taken WITHOUT animation, so it exonerated the MESH but said nothing about the CLIP. The decisive test is the same entry in the viewer WITH the clip Sacred.Rigs picked for it (`--grn=Waldelfe_dark.grn --anim=<picked>`): if it splays there too, the defect is in the clip binding or the clip choice and has nothing to do with the world path at all, and ModelView already reports anim_bound and anim_unbound_names to say which. Note that rigs_check measures every creature clip at score 0.844..1.000, so a grossly wrong clip choice is unlikely and PARTIAL BONE BINDING is the more plausible reading -- but that is a hypothesis, not a finding, and the viewer test is what would settle it. --creatures-noanim is retained as the control; rig_placement.gd is retained because it is correct in itself and harmless, but it is NOT a fix for this.

column4: THE VIEWER TEST SETTLES IT: THE CLIP DISPLACES THE WHOLE MODEL, AND NEITHER THE CLIP CHOICE NOR THE BINDING IS AT FAULT. `--grn=Waldelfe_dark.grn --anim=DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01.GRN` (the clip Sacred.Rigs picks for it, score 0.9762) reports tracks=166 bound=84/88 length=3.966667, and the FOUR unbound names are Bone_weapon_02, Bone_weapon_01, Dummy02, Dummy24 -- weapon attachment points and dummies an unarmed elf has no counterpart for. Partial binding is therefore refuted along with row 759's hypothesis. The rendered frame shows only the model's LEGS, entering from the top of the image: ModelView frames its camera on the BIND pose, and the animated pose has carried the mesh bodily upward out of that frame. In the streamed world the same displacement is what reads as splayed limbs -- parts of the mesh flung away from where PlayerView placed it -- which is why re-ordering the placement write (row 759) could not help.
column5: WHAT THIS POINTS AT, and it is row 609's structural finding arriving from a third direction. ModelView.build_animation skips only the CLIP's own root (parent_effective == -1, i.e. __Root) and binds every other track by name, so the clip's Bip01 POSITION track is applied to the model's Bip01. But row 609 measured that the two files do not share the chain above Bip01: model 589 carries a coordinate-alignment bone ('Root', a 90-degree Z rotation) between __Root and Bip01 that the clip has no node for at all. A position track authored relative to the clip's parent chain, applied onto a bone whose parent chain differs, displaces everything below it -- which is exactly what the frame shows. The same premise underlies rows 605/606/739: world-space composition differs, local per-bone data agrees.
column6: NOT FIXED, AND THE FIX IS A BINDING DECISION RATHER THAN A BUG FIX -- handed over deliberately. The options are (a) bind ROTATION tracks only and drop clip position tracks except for a deliberate root-motion channel, which is the standard retargeting answer when two rigs disagree above the hips, or (b) compensate each position track by the alignment bone's transform so clip-space translations land correctly in model space. (a) is cheaper and testable immediately; (b) preserves authored motion but needs the alignment bone identified per model, which row 609 only established for entry 589. Either changes how EVERY clip plays, so it is not a change to make without a stated pre-specified test -- rig_check.gd and the --creatures-noanim control both exist to measure it. STATE LEFT BEHIND: rig_placement.gd is retained (correct in itself, not a fix for this), --creatures-noanim is retained as the control, and the lit-rig fix of row 757 stands.

column4: ROTATION-ONLY CLIP BINDING IS IN (option (a) of row 760) AND IT FIXES THE DISPLACEMENT, BUT IT DOES NOT FULLY CLEAN UP THE WORLD RIGS. ModelView gained const BIND_POSITION_TRACKS := false; build_animation now skips every clip POSITION track and binds only ROTATION. Track count for DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01.GRN on WALDELFE_DARK.GRN halves from 166 to 83 with bound unchanged at 84/88, which is the expected shape -- one position and one rotation track per bound bone, position dropped. FOUR TESTS WERE STATED BEFORE THE CHANGE RAN. (1) viewer shows a whole figure rather than legs: PASS -- the model is fully framed, coherent, and posed differently from bind (arm forward), so rotation animation is applied. (3) motion survives: PASS -- 1214 pixels differ between t=0 and t=1.5s, confined to the creature bbox (555,28)-(634,538); the fix did not freeze anything. (4) rig_check still passes: PASS, unchanged at topology 59/60 and local rest 47/60 within 0.01 against control 1/26.
column5: TEST (2) FAILS AS STATED, AND I AM RECORDING IT AS A FAILURE RATHER THAN AS A PARTIAL WIN. The pre-stated wording was that world creatures must LOOK LIKE the static --creatures-noanim control. They do not. The gross defect is gone -- the animated figure is an upright, recognisable humanoid where before it was splayed with limbs flung off-body -- but it reads taller than the static control and a thin diagonal streak still trails from the lower figure. So the position tracks were A cause of the corruption and demonstrably the cause of the whole-model displacement the viewer exposed, but they are not the ONLY thing wrong with an animated rig in the world path.
column6: KEPT ANYWAY, with the reason stated: the viewer is now correct, three of four pre-stated tests pass, and the change is a strict improvement over a rig that left its own camera framing. THE COST IS REAL AND IS DOCUMENTED IN THE CONSTANT ITSELF: any authored TRANSLATION in a clip is now dropped, so a lunge, hop or step plays in place, and retail root motion is not reproduced. The upgrade path remains option (b) of row 760 -- per-model alignment-bone compensation, which needs that bone identified per model rather than only for entry 589 as row 609 measured. NEXT MEASUREMENT for whoever resumes: identify what the residual streak is attached to. ModelView reports bound/unbound per clip and the four unbound names here are Bone_weapon_02/01, Dummy02, Dummy24, so a bone left at BIND while its neighbours rotate is the obvious suspect -- unmeasured, and not to be assumed.

column4: THE STREAK IS NOT IDENTIFIED. What IS settled is that row 761's own suspect is WRONG: the four names ModelView reports as anim-unbound for DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01.GRN on WALDELFE_DARK.GRN -- Bone_weapon_01, Bone_weapon_02, Dummy02, Dummy24 -- are CLIP-SIDE bones with no model counterpart. Each returns bone_index=-1 when looked up in the model's own 90-entry bone_names list, so they are bones the clip carries and the model lacks; they drive nothing, no vertex can be weighted to them, and they cannot produce a stray rendered element. 'A bone left at BIND while its neighbours rotate' is therefore refuted for those four, and whatever the streak attaches to is a MODEL bone that the clip does drive.
column5: A SECOND PROBE IN THE SAME RUN PRODUCED NOTHING AND ITS OUTPUT IS DISCARDED RATHER THAN REPORTED. It attempted to count vertices weighted per bone via Sacred.Models.mesh_weights and printed weighted_bones=0, which is not a measurement -- it guessed the returned dictionary's keys as bone_indices/bone_weights when the reader actually exposes bone_map (sacred.gd's own doc comment for mesh_weights describes the FormMeshBone/FormMeshBoneSection chain and the highestBoneIndex+1 pairing). A zero from a wrong key name says nothing about the data.
column6: NEXT MEASUREMENT, stated so it is not re-derived: read mesh_weights' real shape first, then ask which MODEL bones carry vertex weight and which of those the clip does NOT bind a rotation track to -- ModelView.build_animation binds by name, so a weighted model bone whose name has no clip counterpart stays at bind while everything around it rotates, which is the remaining shape that fits a thin trailing element. Note the viewer capture at row 761 showed no obvious streak at its framing, so it may be visible only at the world's smaller on-screen scale, and the comparison should be made in the world against the --creatures-noanim control rather than in the model viewer.

column4: ROW 762'S MEASUREMENT, RUN. Over all 121 creature meshes the spawn tables name, resolved to clips through Sacred.Rigs, EXACTLY ONE model has bones that carry vertex weight and that its chosen clip binds no rotation track to: WALDELFE_DARK.GRN under DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01.GRN leaves Bip01 Ponytail03_01..05 undriven -- a five-segment chain holding 31.67 of 980.0 weight units (3.23%) while the head above it rotates. Thin, trailing, rare: the shape fits the streak, and it is the ONLY candidate of this kind in the whole creature set. NOT YET VISUALLY CONFIRMED as the streak -- the confirming test is a world capture containing WALDELFE_DARK against the --creatures-noanim control, since the row 761 viewer framing showed nothing. TWO GUARDS THE FIRST RUN NEEDED. (1) An unguarded run reported 53 models at 100% unbound; that is an ARTEFACT, not data -- when Sacred.Models.clip fails to decode, clip_track_bone returns empty, the driven set is empty, and every weighted bone looks unbound. Discarded and re-run with an undecodable guard. (2) mesh_weights keys are count/highest/bones/weights/BONE_MAP -- an earlier guess of bone_indices/bone_weights produced weighted_bones=0 and was discarded. SEPARATE FINDING WORTH ITS OWN ROW LATER: 52 of those 121 pairs have an UNDECODABLE clip (Sacred.Models.clip rejects record 0, implied size 256 against span 280, nt=3 nq=3 nu=3), and corpus-wide only 2069 of the motion entries decode at all. THE FORK ROW 762 LEFT IS ANSWERED: retail DOES animate this chain. 1390 decodable clips drive some ponytail-named bone, and 68 drive Ponytail03 specifically with 6 tracks each (AMAZ_HORSE_*, DUEL_*, DUE1_*). So the undriven chain is a property of the clip Rigs CHOSE, not of the format -- Rigs picks by bone geometry, which cannot see that a candidate omits a whole limb. Whether retail itself ever pairs this mesh with this clip is unknown and is the next question.

THE UNDECODABLE CLIPS ARE FIXED. Sacred.Models.clip refused an entry unless every record reconciled to header 52 + 16nt + 20nq + 16nu + a HARDCODED 48-byte trailer. Corpus-wide that trailer is BIMODAL: 2508 motion entries carry 48 and 863 carry 72. The constant came from 05-02, which sampled three clips and drew all-48 -- a real measurement on an unrepresentative sample, not an error. clip() now SOLVES the width per entry (_clip_trailer) and stores it in the returned dict as "trailer". RESULT: decodable motion entries 2069 -> 2738, and the world creature set goes from 52 of 121 pairs with an undecodable clip to 16. NO REGRESSION, and the evidence is exact: the solved-48 population is 2069 entries, which is precisely the set that decoded before. WHERE THE 24 BYTES LIVE, settled by payload and not by arithmetic. A 76-byte header reconciles every size identically to a 72-byte trailer, so sizes cannot choose between them. The translate-track TIMES can: at +52 they start at 0.000 and ascend (DRF1_RUN_1H.GRN record 1: 0.000, 0.059, 0.117, step 0.0587), at +76 they start at 0.352 -- exactly 6 floats = 24 bytes into the same array. Ascending-from-zero holds at +52 for 82810 of 82810 affected records and at +76 for only 76264. Header stays 52; the bytes are trailing. THE SOLVER IS STRICTER THAN THE CONSTANT IT REPLACES, which is the point. An entry with N records gives N-1 independent constraints on one unknown, and because each record has its own nt/nq/nu a wrong header or field-offset layout cannot yield a constant residual -- it yields a spread and is refused. Zero-slack posture unchanged: one byte of disagreement still refuses the WHOLE entry. WOLF_ATTACK_BH_A.GRN (46 records implying 17 different widths) was refused before and is refused now. Single-record entries constrain nothing, so they are held to the two attested widths; the 20 such entries solve to 1728..13560 and stay refused. 683 entries still refuse, for other reasons (unit-quaternion check, 19 internally inconsistent, 20 single-record). ONE HYPOTHESIS REFUTED ALONG THE WAY: that _span_sec over-measured spans by taking the first later node in DIRECTORY order rather than the nearest by ADDRESS. Recomputing every span as the nearest-by-address gave byte-identical output, so the directory is address-sorted and _span_sec is correct. ONE ARTEFACT DISCARDED: an unguarded first pass reported 53 of 121 creature models as 100% weighted-but-unbound; that is what an empty driven set looks like when clip() refuses, not data. Guarded by clip_trailer_check.gd, whose load-bearing assertion is that BOTH widths still occur -- re-hardcoding either constant still decodes thousands of clips and still passes every other check in godot-port, and shows up only as one population collapsing to zero. Full suite green: 21 of 21.

THE STREAK IS FOUND, AND IT IS NOT THE PONYTAIL. Row 763 is REFUTED as an explanation and row 761 is CORRECTED. A one-variable capture pair (--creatures vs --creatures-noanim, same seed, same cell, one named mesh) shows that applying a clip COLLAPSES THE ENTIRE MESH. BEAR.GRN without animation draws a correct quadruped silhouette -- four legs, body, head; with BEAR_* applied it is a thin diagonal line plus a small white blob, diff bbox 106x96. WALDELFE_DARK.GRN without animation is an upright narrow humanoid; with DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01 it is a horizontal diagonal smear with thin spikes radiating out, diff bbox 37x101. The "residual thin diagonal streak" row 762 could not identify IS the animated creature. Five ponytail bones carrying 3.23% of the vertex weight cannot produce this, so the row 763 candidate is refuted as the cause -- it remains a real defect, just not this one. ROW 761 MUST BE READ DOWN: it reported that rotation-only binding "fixes the displacement" with 3 of 4 tests passing and only a cosmetic residual. It does not. Whatever those tests measured, they did not catch that an animated mesh collapses to a line, and no test in godot-port did -- the failure was only ever visible in pixels. GRN animation is broken at the POSE level, not cosmetically, and phase 5 should be treated as open. ROW 763 UNIQUENESS CLAIM WITHDRAWN. Re-running its measurement on the row 764 decoder gives the ponytail IDENTICAL numbers (5 bones, 31.67 of 980.00, 3.23%) but it is no longer the only case: 3 of 121 pairs now have weighted-but-undriven bones where 1 did before, because 52 pairs were excluded by undecodable clips and are now 15. The worst is STACHELALBAUFBLUTSCHRECKE01.GRN under BLUT_WALK_BH.GRN at 60 of 93 bones and 55.17% of the weight -- Pelvis, R Thigh, R Calf, R Foot, Spine, Spine2, Neck all undriven, which is half a body frozen rather than a trailing element. GLORB.GRN under GLOR_DEFEND_BH.GRN is the third at 5.22%. WOLF IS STILL FROZEN: its animated and unanimated captures differ by ZERO pixels (diff bbox 0x0) because the WOLF_* clips are among the 683 entries row 764 still refuses -- they are the internally inconsistent ones, 46 records implying 17 trailer widths. So a wolf in the world is a static mesh, silently. TOOLING: main.gd gained --creatures-only=PREFIX, which filters the sector roll to one mesh and spawns it even where the sector rolls nothing (parsed before the empty-sector return on purpose -- a town sector must not answer "nothing here" when the flag names a mesh to draw). It composes with --creatures-noanim, which is what made a one-variable visual pair possible at all; row 763 called for exactly this comparison and could not run it. Suite still 21 of 21 green, which is itself the finding about the suite.

THE COLLAPSE OF ROW 765 IS FIXED. CAUSE: ModelView.build_animation wrote each clip key straight onto the model bone of the same name. A key is expressed against the CLIP rest, and clip and model do not share one -- row 739 measured their local rests agreeing on only 47 of 60 bones, worst case 6.74 -- so a direct write REPLACES the bone rest orientation with a foreign one, and because a limb inherits its parent error the displacement accumulates outward. FIX: apply the clip motion as a delta against its own rest, pose = model_rest * (clip_rest^-1 * key). MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on BEAR.GRN + BEAR_WALK_BH.GRN, using global_pose * skin_bind, which must be the identity for every bone at the bind pose: worst offset at t=0 falls from 84.71 units to 1.54 on a rig 110 units wide, and the bone bounding box at every sampled t goes from an inflated 134.57x196.57x127.19 to exactly the rest 109.53x196.57x127.19. VISUALLY CONFIRMED: BEAR animated was a thin diagonal line, and is now a correct quadruped in a walk pose, matching its own --creatures-noanim control in silhouette. HOW IT WAS LOCALISED, since three hypotheses died first. (1) Record-to-bone binding is POSITIONAL and unguarded beyond a count check -- refuted, 5855 of 5916 unambiguous records match on the diagonal. An earlier version of that same probe said 70% and was DISCARDED as an artefact: off-diagonal hits at d=0.0000 are TIES, because many bones share an identity rest rotation and argmin picks arbitrarily among them; only unique-by-margin matches carry information. (2) The skeleton is collapsing -- refuted, bone bbox and pose scale stayed sane. (3) The skin is malformed -- refuted, bind is the inverse world bind transform and noanim renders correctly. The measurement that found it was global_pose * skin_bind per bone, which is nonzero at t=0 only if the pose is not the bind pose. ONE HARNESS ARTEFACT DISCARDED: a first probe seeked without ticking and read the rest pose back at every t; AnimationPlayer.seek(t,true) needs a frame, so that run measured the harness, not the rig. NOT CLAIMED: WALDELFE_DARK still looks splayed in its capture. Its numbers are now sane (t=0 offset 1.07, bbox tracking rest, Z 107->81 through the attack), so what is on screen is a lunge I cannot call broken from that framing -- BEAR is the confirmed case, the elf is not verified either way. WOLF STILL CANNOT ANIMATE AT ALL: WOLF_IDLE_BH is among the 683 clips row 764 still refuses, so anim_check reports it SKIPPED rather than passing over it. GUARDED by anim_check.gd. Its property is NOT "every bone is at bind at t=0" -- that was asserted first and is FALSE: a clip first key is usually its own rest but need not be, BEAR_WALK_BH opens 3 of 42 bones off-rest and DRF1_ATTACK_SPECIAL01 opens 30 of 83 off-rest, which is the animation, not an error. The exact property is that a bone whose first key IS its clip rest must land on the MODEL rest and no other bone need, so the expected count is computed from the clip and matched EXACTLY (39==39, 53==53). A THRESHOLD I INVENTED WAS REMOVED RATHER THAN TUNED: the control first demanded a fixed 0.2 gap between retargeted and raw agreement, a number picked before any measurement; BEAR cleared it and the elf came in at 0.13. Lowering it to fit would have been scoring the test after seeing the result, so the control was REFORMULATED to measure its actual intent -- the count of bones whose clip and model rests genuinely differ, i.e. where the retarget is not the identity (BEAR 25, elf 19). Full suite 22 of 22 green.

THERE IS NO CLIP TRAILER. The residual both earlier models absorbed is 24 * numUnknowns, so the "unknown" track element is 40 bytes -- 4 of time plus a 36-byte payload -- and nothing follows the record. implied = 52 + 16nt + 20nq + 40nu reconciles ZERO SLACK on every record of every decodable clip, including all 46 records of WOLF_ATTACK_BH_A where no constant can. HOW IT HID TWICE, which is the transferable part. 05-02 sampled three clips whose records all carried nu=2; 24*2 = 48, which reads exactly like a fixed trailer. Row 764 found entries with nu=3, read 24*3 = 72, and concluded the trailer was BIMODAL -- still a constant, just two of them. Both models fit every entry whose nu never varies, which is nearly all of them. Only a clip whose nu VARIES between records can tell the difference, and row 764 had already refused those as "internally inconsistent" -- the WOLF family, 46 records across 17 apparent widths, was the one shape telling the truth and was discarded as noise. The error was never in the algebra, it was that every confirming entry had a constant nu. RESULT: decodable motion entries 2738 -> 2750, and 4 of 6 WOLF clips decode where 0 did (IDLE_BH, ATTACK_BH_A, RUN_BH, WALK_BH). WOLF_DYING_A and WOLF_HIT_A remain refused -- they are single-record entries, a different shape. 671 entries still refuse and are NOT a size problem: the +12 gain shows almost all of them fail the unit-quaternion check or another gate, which is the next question and is untouched here. CONTENT NOT CLAIMED. 9 floats is the shape of Granny scale-shear 3x3 and that was the working guess; read as a matrix the values are degenerate (WOLF_ATTACK_BH_A gives determinants near zero and NEGATIVE, which no scale-shear has). I had already written that guess into clip_layout_check as a determinant assertion -- it failed, and the assertion was REMOVED rather than loosened, because it asserted a meaning I never measured. The 36 bytes are handed back as raw floats, uninterpreted, and nothing consumes them. WOLF NOT FIXED ON SCREEN. The wolf now animates -- its animated-vs-noanim diff goes from 0x0 (a silently static mesh) to 221x211 -- but the rendered result is a sprawling distorted mass, not a wolf. THE ROW 784 TRAP IS NOW GUARDED IN CODE. ModelView gained freeze_anim(t), which sets speed_scale to 0 and seeks -- the ONLY sanctioned setup for reading a posed skeleton -- plus an anim_frozen property that is true only while the player is genuinely parked (flag set AND speed_scale still 0, so a caller that resumes playback cannot leave a stale claim behind). seek_anim() explicitly CLEARS the flag and is documented as not a freeze, because --creatures relies on it to desynchronise loops and must keep animating; conflating the two is what would reintroduce the bug. sample_bone_pose() now REFUSES with push_error and returns IDENTITY when the player is advancing and not frozen. GUARDED BY anim_freeze_check.gd, which pins all four transitions: a rig with no clip is not frozen, play_clip leaves it RUNNING, freeze_anim parks it, seek_anim un-parks it. THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION IS THE GUARD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: while the player advances sample_bone_pose must return IDENTITY (refusal is observable, since that is what refusing looks like), and once parked it must return something else. Asserting only the frozen half would pass against a reader with no guard at all -- the first version of this check did exactly that and also carried a no-op assertion (x or true), both of which were removed rather than left in as decoration. WHAT THIS CHECK DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: measure a pose. That needs frames, and check.gd.s failsafe (correctly) treats an _init that returns without finish() as a failed assert. A check that needed frames is precisely the check that could not exist while this bug was live, which is why the contract is pinned as an API state machine instead. The complementary design point stands: anim_check reads the ANIMATION rather than the skeleton, which is why it never caught row 784 and why that was the right choice -- pure-data checks have held up all session, scene-based ones have not. Web search establishes correctly that Xvfb never uses a GPU -- "does not support hardware acceleration, and will not make use of your GPU, even if you have one" (openrobots MORSE docs), "will always use mesa software rendering" (NVIDIA forums) -- and this box has two GPUs (/dev/dri/card0, card1, renderD128, renderD129).
