I should have read the process environment before recommending an env var, which is the same failure this session has logged a dozen times in other forms: a plausible mechanism proposed without checking the precondition. SECOND AND MORE USEFUL FACT, unexplained: the live process has NO Mesa DRI driver mapped at all -- no swrast, llvmpipe, iris, radeonsi or zink appears in /proc/<pid>/maps (310 mappings total). For an OpenGL application that is not normal. The launcher preloads xshim.so AHEAD of libGL.so.1 (play.sh line 49, LD_PRELOAD="xshim.so:libGL.so.1"), so whatever GL path the engine takes is going through the shim first, and the slowness is neither Xvfb nor llvmpipe. WHERE A REAL SPEEDUP WOULD COME FROM, if wanted: find out what xshim.so does with GL. It exists because SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11 stalls the engine at dxDriver7::dxDriver7() (AGENTS.md), so it is already substituting for a broken path, and it may be doing so in software. That is a code question about a file in this repo, answerable without any web search or new harness -- and it is the one I should have asked instead of reaching for infrastructure. Guard fix verified meanwhile: with provenance filtering the road route yields exactly the three position offsets 2767728/2767772/2767804 and no cursor words. XSHIM_NOTRACK=1 DOES NOT SURVIVE, exactly as xshim.c.s own comment predicted ("Expect the 2005 double-free to abort somewhere; that is the point of the tracking"). The run reaches SDL_SetVideoMode 1024x768 bpp=32 and schedules its screenshots, then dies with glibc "double free or corruption (out)" before gameplay. Zero frames captured. So the malloc tracking is LOAD-BEARING, not instrumentation overhead: the hash table and its global spinlock exist to absorb a real double-free in the retail binary, and removing them reproduces the bug in under 45 seconds. The speed idea is dead in this form. OPERATIONAL NOTE: the abort leaves the process WEDGED with its window up -- glibc aborts, the game does not exit, and `timeout 75` could not reap it. It needed pkill -9. Any future A/B against the tracker must expect that and kill hard rather than wait. WHAT THIS CLOSES, and it is a chain of three wrong guesses of mine in a row, each cheaper to check than the last: Xvfb was not the bottleneck (row 818 -- the runs were already on DISPLAY=:0); llvmpipe was not the bottleneck (no Mesa DRI driver is mapped at all; xshim.c states rendering goes through SDL3.s EGL/Wayland path); and now the malloc tracker cannot simply be switched off. The 1fps remains UNEXPLAINED and the three cheapest explanations are eliminated. WHERE TO LOOK NEXT, if speed is still wanted: the tracker can be made cheap WITHOUT being removed -- the global spinlock is the suspicious part, since a single-threaded 2005 game contends with nothing and the lock is pure overhead on every malloc and free. Making lock()/unlock() no-ops (leaving the hash table intact) preserves the double-free protection while deleting the atomic traffic, and is a two-line experiment with the same A/B shape. If that does not move the framerate, the cost is the hash table itself and the next step is measuring it rather than guessing again -- XSHIM_STATS already exists and dumps allocation counts. Suite 23 of 23 green, decodable 3413 of 3421, working tree verified.

XSHIM_NOLOCK=1 ADDED AND IT SURVIVES. xshim.c.s lock()/unlock() become no-ops when set, leaving the hash table -- and therefore the double-free protection -- fully intact. Ran the load-a-save script with it: both scheduled screenshots captured, no abort, clean shutdown. That is the predicted outcome and the reason this experiment is safe where XSHIM_NOTRACK=1 was not (row 819 reproduced the 2005 double-free in under 45s by removing the live-set itself). The rationale: this engine is single-threaded on this stack, so every malloc and free pays an atomic read-modify-write that nothing ever contends. SPEED IS NOT MEASURED AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED. The script used only loads a save; nothing in it measures throughput, so all that is established is SAFETY. Saying "it survives, therefore it is faster" would be exactly the inference this session has spent nineteen rows retracting -- a plausible mechanism reported as a result without the measurement that separates them. THE MEASUREMENT IS SMALL AND SHOULD COME NEXT: autopilot already hooks SDL_GL_SwapBuffers, so a frame counter is a one-line static incremented there and printed at each SACRED_SHOT time. That gives frames-per-interval directly, and the A/B is one run with XSHIM_NOLOCK and one without, same script, comparing counts. Until that runs, XSHIM_NOLOCK is an available switch of unknown benefit, not a speedup. If it shows no gain, the cost is the hash table rather than the lock, and XSHIM_STATS already dumps allocation counts to size it. ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT NOTHING IS CACHED. Built ztrace.so, a 32-bit shim interposing inflate() that fingerprints each call.s INPUT (length plus first 32 bytes) and counts fingerprint recurrence. Gameplay measurement: 220000 inflate calls in 80s, 219443 of them REPEATS -- 99.7% -- against only 557 distinct streams. That is roughly 400 re-inflations of every stream, at ~2750 inflate calls per second, and the bytes_in counter wrapping past 4GB (32-bit unsigned long) puts the redundant volume in the many gigabytes. The engine decompresses the same small working set over and over, every frame, forever. IT EXPLAINS ROW 823 EXACTLY. zlib-ng is 2-4x on inflate yet bought only 29%, which did not fit a throughput-bound model. It fits this one perfectly: the cost is not how fast a stream inflates, it is that ~550 streams are inflated 400 times each. No library swap can fix a missing cache, and the 29% is simply the fraction of the work that WAS throughput. THE FINGERPRINT IS DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE: 32 bytes plus length, not a full hash, so a collision would make two DIFFERENT streams look identical and thereby OVERSTATE repeats. But the direction of that bias is the point -- to be wrong here the fingerprint would have to be colliding at 99.7%, which 32 bytes of real compressed data does not do. A false "no cache" reading cannot come from the instrument. SCOPE, and it matters: this is a property of the RETAIL ENGINE, measured in the retail binary. It is not a finding about godot-port, and the port must NOT replicate it -- Sacred.Pak/Models already decode on demand, and anything built on them should keep decoded results rather than inheriting a 2005 pathology by imitation. Under canonical-first the port reproduces retail.s VISIBLE behaviour and its flaws, not its performance bugs. PRACTICAL CEILING: at 99.7% redundancy the theoretical headroom is enormous -- a working cache of ~550 streams would remove almost all of the 78% CPU row 822 measured -- but implementing one means interposing at the engine.s asset layer, not at inflate(), since inflate() cannot know what the caller will do with the output. That is a much larger piece of work than a shim and is not obviously worth it: 1.5fps already completes every scripted run this session needed. Suite 23 of 23 green, decodable 3413 of 3421.

THE WIDE TAG PAYLOADS ARE DECODED: A 12-BYTE TAG IS THREE SIGNED i32, AND THE 'HUGE' DECIMAL VALUES IN EVERY EARLIER DUMP WERE THAT STRUCT PRINTED AS ONE INTEGER. Control arm, run over all 16 files and 1.35M records: read the same 12 bytes as i32 at byte offsets 0..4 and score in-range. Aligned reads score 100.0%, misaligned 0.0-0.4% (offsets 5-8 were DISCARDED as a bad control -- the third field is near-zero so any read landing in it passes trivially, and the agent said so rather than banking it). Six-u16 is refuted for the coordinate tags: the odd u16 slots are constant 0 or 0xFFFF, i.e. sign-extension high halves. SIGNED, not unsigned -- 4294967073 is -223. The two examples that motivated the question reproduce byte-exactly: 27127013446221 = tag04{4685, 6316, 0}, a chest at cell (4685,6316); 75557863725931503288324 = tag35{4, 4, 4096}; 4294967359 = tag34(63, 1) as 2xi32. COORDINATE TAGS: 0x04 (129,477 occurrences, cell_x, cell_y, enum), 0x0d (7,060, field2 always 0), 0x2a (43,491), 0x4d (393 of 415). Corroboration is independent of range-fitting: op23's known plain-int coordinates and tag 0x04's literals are DISJOINT populations that hit the same ceiling near 6328, and tag-0x04 points fall in op23-occupied spatial bins at 4.0x (bin 128), 9.5x (64), 14x (32) and 23x (16) over a uniform-random control on the same bounding box. TAG 0x20 IS A SECOND COORDINATE SYSTEM AT SUB-CELL PRECISION, and it was decoded by regression rather than assertion: 0x20 never co-occurs with op23 but always co-occurs with 0x04 (85,227 records carry both), slopes are 53.669 (x) and 53.667 (y), a divisor grid-search over 53.0..54.5 in steps of 0.002 peaks sharply at 53.666 (88.6% floor-match, against 71.8% at 53.670 and 66.9% at 53.660), and the exact rational form t04 == t20*3//161 holds for 84.7% x / 89.1% y while //54 gives 0.6% and //53 gives 0.06%. The residual sits between 0.04 and 0.91 from p10 to p90 -- exactly a fractional position inside the cell. So 161 fine units per 3 cells, 53 and 2/3 per cell. OTHER 12-BYTE TAGS: 0x19 (140,048; id<=1249, weight<=100, flag -- repeats within a record, i.e. a weighted drop or spawn table, consistent with rows 728-729), 0x35 (53,118; field2 = 4096 in 53,090 of them), 0x0c (8,775; MIXED absolute and relative -- 28.9% are negative and every negative is small, -3..-500 with median -50, while positives look absolute with median ~3987, and per-record disambiguation is UNDER-DETERMINED, not solved). 8-byte tags 0x33/0x34/0x87/0x88/0x89 are all 2xi32 small paired scalars, none coordinates. NOT DECODED, and left that way rather than guessed: 0x15 (2xi32 vs 4xu16 both plausible, only 44 distinct values, the agent declined to call it), 0x79 (f0 = 0x00FFFFFF in >75%, f1 in {1,4} -- smells like RGB+flag with nothing to corroborate it), 0x3c (78 occurrences, 51 all-zero), 0x3d (ZERO occurrences in all 16 files -- untestable, not unsolved). FIELD 2 OF EVERY COORDINATE TAG is a 0..4 enum; that it is NOT a coordinate is solid, what it means (map layer, dungeon storey, orientation) is a guess and is not being made. TWO CAVEATS ON THIS ROW, both mine. (1) I briefed the agent that world cells run 0..12800; it measured 0..6330 and corrected me. But row 804 places script content at cells up to 10112,7296, so ~6330 is the extent of THESE tags' values, NOT the extent of the world, and should not be quoted as a world bound. (2) The tag-0x04 string-form label resolution rate reads 100% (1,811/1,811) in row 832 and 24.0% (of 44,028) here. Not a contradiction: row 832 measured op1/op8 in startcode.bin only, where labels are file-local; this figure is corpus-wide including funkcode, where most references are cross-file. Both controls hold (row 832's other-string-operand control at 0-2.2%; this one's all-other-string-tags control at 3.4%, a 7-11x enrichment). Do not merge the two numbers.

A REAL PARSER DEFECT, AND THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS OF IT WAS WRONG. A subagent reported that tag 0x4d 'needs VARIANT/string handling it does not have', on the evidence of 22 records whose 0x4d payload is the ASCII text axVerstecke_. TESTED THAT DIRECTLY: adding 0x4d to the VARIANT table is INERT -- the 0xfffffffe sentinel branch never fires for it, 330 occurrences and 0 string-form, and the all-files sweep is 1,123,758 records / 0 unparsed both before and after. So the change was not made. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, from the raw record body (elve/funkcode.bin op 58, offset 0xee8e): 48 ff ff ff ff 'AnzahlVerstecke\0' 'MaxVerstecke_r+Var(RNr)\0'. Tag 0x48 is NUMSTR, so it consumes the u32 and the FIRST string and stops. The parser then reads the next byte -- 'M', which is 0x4d -- as a TAG, and 0x4d's 12-byte width swallows the front of the second string. axVerstecke_ is simply MaxVerstecke_ with its M eaten. So 0x48 takes TWO strings after its u32, which is exactly the shape row 721 proved for tag 0x3a (two strcpy calls in one handler), and 0x4d is an innocent bystander whose byte value happens to be the letter M. SCOPE: 16 occurrences across all 16 files, all with the identical 12 bytes, in opcodes 58 and 66. They do not fail the parse -- ok stays True because trailing garbage is absorbed -- which is precisely the hollow-metric failure the parser's own docstring warns about, and is why this survived rows 711-726. THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT, not run here: disassemble handler 0x0826cb0e (the NUMSTR handler serving 0x48/0x49/0x4a/0x5d/0x5e/0x6d/0x6e) and count strcpy calls, as row 721 did for 0x3a. TWO strcpys confirms; one refutes and forces a different reading. NOT CHANGING THE PARSER ON THE INFERENCE ALONE -- 0x48 is 70,000+ occurrences and a wrong width there would silently reshape far more than the 16 records it fixes. The correct arm is the handler, and it is cheap.

It decodes opcodes 23, 1 and 8 only, walking past the rest by their length field, with a WIDTH table censused from those three opcodes' actual tags across all 16 files -- an unlisted tag inside one of them is a parse ERROR, the same refusal Sacred.Funk makes, because a shifted cursor turns model ids into plausible nonsense rather than into a crash. Two passes, because an op1 record may name a position declared later in the file. INDEPENDENT-IMPLEMENTATION PARITY, which is the real verification here: the GDScript reader reproduces the Python reference exactly, including the control rate to the record (58/107). Per-class counts all match: 2,565 NPCs and 16,021 objects over the eight classes, 49 distinct body models, 29 distinct main-hand items, unresolved named positions ZERO in every class. THE CHECK'S FIRST NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS VACUOUS AND I REPLACED IT. It fed the join the position tag's LAYER field, which scored 0.9% -- but only because that field is a 0..4 enum sitting near zero, so it could not have failed. The informative control is the record's own CELL_X: a world coordinate, definitively not a model id, which resolves to a .grn 54.2% of the time because .grn records occupy items ids 0..8191 at 34.9% density and coordinates land squarely in that range. So the check now asserts the control is INSIDE 0.30..0.80 -- too high means the join cannot discriminate, too low means the control has gone vacuous again. A control that cannot fail is not a control, and that is now enforced rather than remembered. MUTATION-TESTED, not assumed: changing _ids() to take the first 4-byte numeric argument instead of the first tag-0x02 one -- exactly the positional reading that produced row 831's bad evidence -- makes the check FAIL. Note WHICH assertion caught it: 'every body id resolves to a .grn' still passed at 1.000 under the mutation, and the DISJOINT body/main-hand name sets is what fired, printing SOLDIER.GRN, HORSE.GRN, SERAPHIM.GRN, ORC_CHAMA.GRN and DARKELVE.GRN as overlapping. THE HANDLER SETTLES ROW 836, AND THE MECHANISM IS NOT THE ONE I INFERRED. Row 836 predicted that tag 0x48 takes TWO strings unconditionally, on the model of 0x3a (row 721: two strcpy calls in one handler), and deliberately refused to change the parser on the inference alone because 0x48 has 46,511 occurrences. Disassembled the NUMSTR handler 0x0826cb0e (serving 0x48/0x49/0x4a/0x5d/0x5e/0x6d/0x6e) with objdump over install/sacred_orig. IT CONTAINS EXACTLY ONE strcpy, at 0x0826cb77 -- so the row 836 prediction is REFUTED as stated, and the second string is reached by a different route. The handler: advance 1 past the tag, read a u32 into the numeric slot [+0xa86c], advance 4, strlen+strcpy the first string into the string slot [+0xa46c], advance len+1. THEN TWO GATES, in this order. First 0x0826cb96 `cmp DWORD PTR [edi+ecx*4+0xa868],0 / jns 0x0826e8b9` -- a SIGNED test on the slot it just wrote (the +4 index difference is the same slot; the index was incremented at 0x0826cb29), so a non-negative u32 ends the tag right there and the common case is untouched. Second 0x0826cba4 `cmp BYTE PTR [eax+ebx],0 / je epilogue` -- the byte after the first string must be non-zero. Only then does it take a SECOND NUL-terminated string, and at 0x0826ccfb it advances the cursor by that string's len+1, which is what makes the record body-exact. WHAT THE SECOND STRING IS, from the code that consumes it: strstr against the constant at 0x086f3468, which is the single character '+' (0x0826cbec); then a loop over the std::string vector at +0x7550 comparing lengths and contents (operator+ at 0x08655400, size at 0x086553d2); then at 0x0826cc40 the RESULT IS WRITTEN BACK OVER THE SENTINEL IN THE SAME NUMERIC SLOT [+0xa868]. So a negative u32 there is not a value at all -- it means THE OPERAND IS THE VARIABLE NAMED IN THE STRING THAT FOLLOWS, resolved at load from a '+'-joined expression. The record row 836 misread, funkcode.bin op 58 at 0xee8e, is `48 ffffffff 'AnzahlVerstecke' 'MaxVerstecke_r+Var(RNr)'` -- an expression, exactly as the '+' needle predicts. There is also a debug printf on this path (0x0826cbba, format string 'test: %s\n'). SCOPE MEASURED BEFORE THE EDIT, which is the point of measuring it: 22 NUMSTR operands out of 46,511 across all 16 files carry a negative u32 -- 0xffffffff in every one, opcodes 58 and 66, strings AnzahlVerstecke and AnzahlVersteckeUW. So the blast radius is 22 records in 1.36 million, not the 46,511 that a wrong unconditional two-string reading would have reshaped. PARSER CHANGED, tools/formats/startcode.py, gated on `u32 & 0x80000000 and the next byte is non-zero` to mirror both engine tests. Before/after over all files: record count 1,360,204 identical, NUMSTR u32 count 46,511 identical, negative count 22 identical -- nothing outside the 22 moved. The third operand of those 22 changed from the integer 29523684567560784455075788897 -- which was tag 0x4d's 12-byte width swallowing the front of the second string, the 'axVerstecke_' artefact of row 836 -- to the string 'MaxVerstecke_r+Var(RNr)'. Those records are now BODY-EXACT: body is 45 bytes and consumption is 1+4+16+24 = 45. All-files sweep still 0 unparsed. NO ENGINE CHANGE NEEDED and I checked rather than assumed: godot-port/formats/startcode.gd censuses widths only from opcodes 23/1/8, and 0x48 does not occur in them; checks/startcode_check.gd re-run is unchanged and PASSES -- 2565 NPCs over 8 classes, 49 bodies, 29 main-hand, body slot 1.000 vs coordinate control 0.542 (58/107). NOT DONE: the sibling NUMSTR handler 0x0826de28 (tag 0x7a) was NOT disassembled, so whether it has the same sentinel path is unknown -- 0x7a has no negative-u32 occurrences in the corpus, so it is untestable from data and only the handler can say. Also unread: what the symbol vector at +0x7550 is populated from, which is the same question as where script variables live at runtime.

AUDITED WHETHER THE RESEARCH IS PROVEN OR MERELY WRITTEN DOWN, BY MUTATING WHAT THE GATES CLAIM TO PROVE. Inventory first: ~209 discrete claims over 15 documents, and the proof coverage is uneven -- pax-saves cites 4 runnable proofs, world-sectors 3, granny-grn and pak-containers 2, while balance-bin, script-bytecode, combat-formulas, tech-stack, build-survey, naming-oracle and decompilation-coverage cite NONE. Mapping the 24 gates onto the readers they exercise corrects part of that -- script-bytecode is in fact covered by four gates, the document simply never names them -- and exposes the inverse gap: Sacred.Creatures, Sacred.Factions and Sacred.Items are exercised by TEN gates and have NO research document at all. Proven code, unwritten claims. THEN THE REAL TEST, because a passing gate proves nothing unless it would fail on a false claim: 14 mutations of documented constants, 12 caught. KEY_OFF 236->232, CELL 32->33, KEY_REC 768->776 and PAK_HDR 256->260 each kill both floor_check and static_chain_check; trigger_check's target offset +6 caught at +5, +7 and +8; creature_check's REC 86 and DATA 256 both caught; clip_layout_check's 3413 decodable clips caught. THE ONE THAT SURVIVED IS THE FINDING. world-sectors.md states floor.pak's +0x04 splits 17/15, low seventeen bits the art tile and top fifteen the mask. Mutating the low mask to 0xffff fails the gate, so the low boundary is pinned -- but changing `v >> 17` to `v >> 16` PASSED. floor_check's two assertions about the high field are that it resolves to a valid tiles.pak index and that tiles.orientation(hi) == hi %% 18. NEITHER CAN FAIL: measured with the project's own reader rather than a third ad-hoc one (my hand-rolled read of tiles.pak disagreed with the documented record count, 107031 against 90132, and was discarded), the identity orientation(i) == i %% 18 holds for 90,132 of 90,132 indices -- every valid one -- and a doubled small id stays under the count. A test that cannot fail, exactly the hollow metric discipline.md names, sitting inside a gate that has been green for days. So the top-15-bits half of that claim was INFERRED, not proven, and the document said otherwise. WHAT SETTLES IT is not a better statistic but a structural invariant: the two fields must partition the u32 with no shared bit, so (low17 | hi<<17) must reconstruct v exactly, which only a 17/15 split does. Added to floor_check; all three boundary mutations -- `v >> 16`, `hi << 16`, LOW17 0xffff -- are now caught, and the document says the boundary was unproven until today. ONE MORE WEAKNESS RECORDED, NOT FIXED: rigs_check asserts a resolved fraction above 0.5 while the actual value is 0.976, so both loosening to 0.05 and tightening to 0.95 pass. It has no control arm, which means it detects catastrophe but not regression and cannot distinguish a correct rig mapping from a dense clip id space -- the same defect row 837 found and fixed in startcode_check. Left open deliberately rather than redesigned on the spot.

ROW 845 LEFT rigs_check WITH A RATE AND NO CONTROL; IT NOW HAS ONE, AND THE CONTROL IS ITSELF MUTATION-TESTED. The defect: the gate asserted a resolved fraction above 0.5 while the measured value is 0.976, so loosening the bar to 0.05 and tightening it to 0.95 both passed, and nothing answered the only question that matters -- what would this score IF THE HYPOTHESIS WERE FALSE. 121 of 124 meshes resolving is equally consistent with a discriminating comparison and with a clip corpus dense enough that anything matches something. THE CONTROL IS A PERMUTATION, not a cross-pairing. Each mesh's bone ORIGINS are rotated by one among that mesh's own sorted bone NAMES, so the comparison sees the same bones, the same names, the same set of positions and the same counts -- `matched` is identical and the denominator cannot shrink -- and the only thing destroyed is the name-to-position correspondence, which is exactly what is under test. CROSS-PAIRING WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED WITH A REASON: creatures genuinely share rigs, which is the entire reason Sacred.Rigs exists, so scoring mesh A against mesh B's clip can be CORRECT, and a control that can accidentally be right is not a control. RESULT: real pairs score 0.844 and above, permuted pairs 0.489 and below, over 20 sampled pairs; the gate fails if the distributions come within 0.20. The permuted figure is far higher than the 0.04 the old comment quoted for a wrong-character pair, which is informative in itself -- rotating among sorted names often lands a bone on a neighbour's position, so roughly half still fall inside the 0.01 tolerance. The separation is 0.355 and does not depend on the margin being tuned. THE CONTROL WAS MUTATION-TESTED, which is the step that distinguishes a control from a decoration: blinding the score to position so every bone counts as within, opening the tolerance from 0.01 to 1000, and making the permutation a NO-OP so the control equals the real arm are all CAUGHT. That last one enforces structurally what row 837 could only remember -- a control that has quietly stopped controlling now fails the check. The check also re-scores each mesh against its own chosen clip independently and asserts agreement with what Sacred.Rigs stored, which is a second decoder for the score itself. REPRODUCIBLE COLD: the rig map is cached in user://, so the run that produced these numbers was repeated with the cache deleted -- 14.3 seconds instead of 0, and identical figures. MIN_RESOLVED_FRAC moved 0.5 -> 0.90, since at 0.5 the bar sat 47 points below the measured value and could detect only catastrophe. Regression: 23 of 24 gates pass, the exception being pax_check correctly refusing without SACRED_CHARS.

SWEPT THE REMAINING GATES BY MUTATION AND FOUND A HARNESS HOLE UNDER THEM, WORSE THAN ANY OF THE WEAK ASSERTIONS IT WAS LOOKING FOR. Eleven gates that had never been mutation-tested got one falsifying change each: armour WANT_GROUPS 85->84, defpos REC 100->96, factions TIER 6->5, spawn CREATURE_REC 86->85, spawn_factions TIER 6->5, trigger REC 16->15 and static_chain HEADS 777->778 are all CAUGHT. Four survived, and sorting them apart mattered more than the count. TWO WERE FALSE ALARMS: goaltick's GOAL_AT_OFFSET cancels by design -- the check sets pending_goal_tick from the same constant it then expects, so any value should hold, and the claim is 'the sim fires on the tick it was ASKED to'; desyncing the request from the expectation is CAUGHT. interior_swap's and door_transition's SECT are coordinate helpers, not claims; falsifying their real verdicts -- a FLOOR cell expected EXTERIOR, and entering a door expected NOT to open the interior -- is CAUGHT in both. THE FOURTH WAS REAL AND GENERAL. Changing footprint_bind_check's expected REGION_KEY from 50039000 to 50039001 makes TWO assertions fail, printing SCRIPT ERROR with full backtraces, and the check STILL PRINTS OK AND EXITS 0. GDScript reports a failed assert() inside a FUNCTION and then returns; _init carries on to its OK line and calls finish(0). check.gd's failsafe only detects '_init never reached finish()', so it is structurally blind to this -- and this is worse than the hang that file was written to fix, because a hang is at least visible while this reports success. EIGHT ASSERTIONS ACROSS FOUR CHECKS sat behind the hole: armour_check 2, footprint_bind_check 2, rig_check 2, rigs_check 2 -- and the rigs_check pair are the BEAR/WOLF spot checks whose own comment says they exist so that a human reading the line knows something is wrong, which no aggregate fraction conveys. They could never fail. Note the timing: row 846 documented those spot checks as the human-readable half of that gate one hour before this measured that they were inert. THE FIX is expect() on check.gd -- records the failure, prints CHECK FAILED, and makes finish() exit 1 no matter what code it is handed, returning the condition so a caller can still bail early and collecting every failure in a run rather than stopping at the first. All eight converted. The three mutations that previously survived are now CAUGHT: wrong region key, BEAR animated as WOLF, wrong armour group count. Regression 23 of 24, the exception pax_check refusing without SACRED_CHARS. GENERAL LESSON, and the reason this was invisible for as long as it was: every one of these gates was GREEN, and greenness is what a mutation test measures against. A suite that has never been mutated is a suite whose failure mode has never been observed.

THE SWEEP IS NOW COMPLETE: every one of the 24 gates has had at least one falsifying mutation applied and caught. The eight never previously swept -- anim, anim_freeze, bindagree, clickmove, equip, items_sprite, pax, rig -- all hold. anim_check catches a broken retarget in all three forms tried (inverted clip_rest*model_rest^-1, identity, and the inverse dropped entirely); anim_freeze catches the freeze flag being set the wrong way round at either of its two sites; bindagree catches LOCAL_WITHIN 0.01 -> 100; rig_check catches WANT_LOCAL_WITHIN 47 -> 40 and WANT_MATCHED 60 -> 55; items_sprite catches a one-off in either the sprite id or the item name; clickmove catches the simulation being skipped entirely; pax catches its corpus variable being renamed. THE FALSE ALARM, AND IT WAS MINE. A first pass reported that disabling retargeting was caught by NOTHING -- three gates green with `retarget := Quaternion()`. That was wrong: the sed pattern contained an unescaped `*`, so `model_rest * clip_rest` was read as a regex meaning 't' followed by zero-or-more spaces and MATCHED NOTHING. The mutation was never applied and I was reading a pristine tree three times over. Proved rather than assumed: the unescaped pattern substitutes 0 occurrences, the escaped one substitutes 1. This is the fourth instrument failure of my own making today, after the eh_frame denominator, the desynced objdump and the wrong VA-to-offset helper, and the pattern is consistent -- every one was an ad-hoc read that the project's own tooling would have got right. LOOSENINGS ARE NOT MUTATIONS, which cost a round to notice: MIN_AT_BIND 0.9->0.1, MIN_TRACKS 20->2, PASS_OWN 0.8->0.1 and MIN_MATCHED 20->2 all 'survived', but a loosened threshold cannot fail by construction and says nothing. Reading what those gates actually measure showed they are strong for a reason that has nothing to do with the threshold: equip_check carries its own control arm (own=0.9859 against cross=0.0556, rule own > 0.80 AND own > 5x cross) and bindagree_check runs a positive and a negative case side by side (piece 207 at 0.918, piece 1 at 0.0400). Both were doing the thing row 846 had to add to rigs_check, and had been doing it all along. anim_check is also insensitive to the retarget AT t=0 by construction -- its own comment says the delta is the identity there because a clip's first key is its rest in 5855 of 5916 records -- yet it still catches every retarget mutation, because its expected count is computed from the clip and compared exactly. CLOSED THE LAST OPEN QUESTION ON THE SCRIPT TAG TABLE, AFTER FIRST TALKING MYSELF INTO A CORRECTION THAT WAS WRONG. Opening the pre-analysed Ghidra project with the vendored 12.1.2 gave a working decompiler for the first time. Reading the tag dispatcher there put the jump tables at 0x086ed31c and 0x086ed5f8 and the NUMSTR handlers at 0x0826bc39 and 0x0826cf35, none of which match the document, so I edited the document. That was the error: the Ghidra project holds sacred-1.0.02-final, while every tool and every document in this repository is written against install/sacred_orig, a build whose .rodata sits exactly 0x6ca0 HIGHER. Checked at the documented addresses in sacred_orig and they are all correct -- 0x086f4298 gives 141 sane entries and 124 distinct handlers, 0x086f3fbc gives 162 entries and 52 handlers -- so the edits were reverted. The finding itself survives the correction and is stronger for it, because it now rests on two builds rather than one. Tag 0x7a is NUMSTR, u32 then NUL-string, advance len+6, arithmetic identical to its seven siblings, but its handler has NO negative-sentinel second string; its tail is a strncasecmp of the string it just wrote against res: followed by a base-10 strtol of the remainder, which is where a res:N operand becomes a resource id. The two builds disassemble instruction-for-instruction alike at 0x0826de28 and 0x0826cf35, and their res: literals sit 0x6ca0 apart, the same shift. A corpus probe confirms the data cannot decide it: 0 of 2053 0x7a operands carry a negative u32 against the siblings' 22, independently reproducing row 838's count. startcode.py now gates the second string on tag != 0x7a, provably inert on every shipped record and still the rule the interpreter implements.

THE WORKSPACE HAS THREE LGP LINUX BINARIES AND NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS WHICH ONE AN ADDRESS BELONGS TO, WHICH IS HOW I SPENT AN ITERATION CONFIDENTLY CORRECTING A DOCUMENT THAT WAS RIGHT. install/sacred_orig (md5 1e888a38) is what opcodes.py and tagwidths.py read and what every address in research/ is written against; install/sacred is byte-identical to lgp-2010/sacred-1.0.02-patched (a1230334) and is what vtables.py takes by default; lgp-2010/sacred-1.0.02-final (952920ab) is what the pre-analysed Ghidra project contains. sacred_orig's .rodata sits exactly 0x6ca0 higher than the other two, so a transplanted .rodata address lands on plausible data and fails silently: 0x086f4298 is the opcode jump table in sacred_orig, with 141 sane entries and 124 distinct handlers, and in the other two it is 88 sane-looking entries of nothing, first entry repeated six times. .text is NOT a uniform shift -- the same tag handler is 0x0826de28 in sacred_orig and 0x0826cf35 in -final, a gap of 0xef3, while the tag table's first entry differs by 0xecf -- so there is no mechanical translation between them and each finding has to be re-read in the reference binary. analysis/rtti/lgp_linux_vmethods.tsv carries no binary in its name and belongs to install/sacred: 2413 of 2413 of its addresses are exact function entries there, 29 of 2413 in sacred_orig. Regenerating the equivalent for sacred_orig and importing it took that program from 730 named functions to 2919, and 2186 of 2189 addresses landed exactly on boundaries Ghidra had found independently, which is a cross-check the vtable walk had never had. The rule is now written at the top of tools/binary/README.md: sacred_orig is the citation standard, verify there before writing anything down.

THE PROJECT HAD A 669MB PRE-ANALYSED GHIDRA DATABASE AND NO GHIDRA POINTED AT IT, SO NOTHING HAD EVER BEEN DECOMPILED. The vendored 12.1.2 opens it, and tools/binary/ghidra/ now reaches it from the shell: decompiled C for an address, annotated disassembly, jump-table dumps, and an importer that seeds a program with the vtable names so the C is readable at all. Seeding sacred_orig took it from 730 named functions to 2919, and CheckNames.java is the gate on that -- it reports how many of a TSV's addresses are exact function entries before anything is written, which is what catches a TSV from the wrong binary (2186/2189 right, 29/2413 wrong). The structural result is that an opcode handler is a seven-instruction trampoline to exactly one implementation function, so naming 141 opcodes is naming 116 functions, and 17 of the 141 point at the shared default and are therefore explicitly ignored rather than merely absent. Harvesting strings reachable from each implementation within three calls, skipping any callee with more than eight callers so a shared utility cannot drown the signal, puts 48 of the 116 bodies within reach of a name against the 34 named today -- op 24 walks a group counting live creatures, op 91 opens the blacksmith and inventory windows, op 92 teleports a figure without a listener, op 98 sets up a sector's ambience, op 104 resolves SOUND_FX_%s and complains about unknown sound types, op 106 reports a missing dialog. None of those are claimed yet: this run produced the instrument and the shortlist, not the names, and the naming oracle still wants the behavioural arm to agree before any of them is written down.

Rewriting 539 rows of research history to make a gate green would destroy the record to satisfy a contract written after it, so tools/parity/log_check.py is a RATCHET: the non-conforming count is pinned at 539 and may only fall, the field contract is enforced strictly from row 661 where the four-field schema becomes continuous, and row 827 is grandfathered by name as the one later row that never adopted it.
